questions.explain: Key: B. A plotter is an output device designed to draw large, precise technical drawings such as plans and maps; a scanner is an input device.

questions.stem:
Which of the following devices can function as BOTH an input device and an output device?

I. Touchscreen
II. Smartphone
III. Scanner
IV. Speaker
questions.explain: Key: C. A touchscreen and a smartphone both accept input (taps, gestures) and display output on the same screen. A scanner is input only and a speaker is output only.

questions.stem: Ms Gumbs needs to carry a 2 GB presentation from her office computer to a classroom computer that has NO internet connection. Which storage medium is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: D. A USB flash drive is portable and easily holds 2 GB. A CD holds only about 700 MB, and cloud storage needs an internet connection.

questions.stem: Which type of memory loses its contents when the computer is switched off?
questions.explain: Key: C. RAM (random access memory) is volatile: it holds data only while the computer has power. ROM, hard disks and flash drives keep their contents.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of operating system software?
questions.explain: Key: C. Android is an operating system that coordinates a device's hardware and runs apps; Excel, Publisher and PowerPoint are application software.

questions.stem:
Items 18–19 refer to the following scenario.

Shanice is a data-entry clerk at an insurance office in Holetown. She keys in claim forms for up to six hours a day without a break. She now complains of pain, numbness and tingling in her wrists and fingers.

Which of the following conditions is Shanice MOST likely experiencing?
questions.explain: Key: B. Pain and tingling in the wrists and fingers caused by long periods of repeated keying are typical of repetitive strain injury (RSI).

questions.stem:
Items 18–19 refer to the following scenario.

Shanice is a data-entry clerk at an insurance office in English Harbour. She keys in claim forms for up to six hours a day without a break. She now complains of pain, numbness and tingling in her wrists and fingers.

Which of the following measures would help to reduce Shanice's symptoms?

I. Using a wrist rest
II. Taking regular short breaks
III. Increasing the brightness of the screen
IV. Keeping her wrists level with the keyboard
questions.explain: Key: B. A wrist rest, regular breaks and level wrists all reduce strain on the wrists. Screen brightness affects the eyes, not the wrists.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way to protect office computers from sudden power spikes during a thunderstorm?
options: Connect the equipment through a surge protector
questions.explain: Key: B. A surge protector shields the computer and peripherals from sudden increases in voltage; the other measures do not deal with power spikes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST environmentally responsible way for a school to dispose of twenty old computer monitors?
options: Throw them into a skip behind the school
Leave them in a storeroom until space runs out
Hand them to an approved e-waste recycler
Dump them at the landfill with general garbage
questions.explain: Key: C. Monitors contain materials that can harm the environment, so they should go to an approved e-waste recycler rather than a landfill or skip.

questions.stem: Which word processing feature combines a standard letter with a list of names and addresses to produce a personalised copy for every customer?
questions.explain: Key: B. Mail merge combines a main document with a data source (such as a spreadsheet or database list) to produce personalised letters, envelopes or labels.

questions.stem: Which feature should be used so that the company name and page number appear at the bottom of EVERY page of a report?
questions.explain: Key: C. A footer is text placed in the bottom margin that repeats on every page; a header repeats in the top margin.

questions.stem: Kareem wants each new chapter of his report to begin at the top of a new page, even if text is added to the chapter before it. Which of the following should he insert before each chapter heading?
questions.explain: Key: A. A page break forces the text that follows to start on a new page, no matter how much text comes before it.

questions.stem: Which type of tab stop should be set to line up a column of money amounts such as 1,250.75 and 98.50 by their decimal points?
questions.explain: Key: C. A decimal tab aligns figures on the decimal point, which is the standard way of displaying money amounts in a column.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT

A 12-page tourist brochure has been typed for a tour company. The supervisor notices that the name of the capital has been spelt ‘Phillipsburg’ in 37 places. It should be ‘Philipsburg’.

Which feature would correct ALL 37 errors in the QUICKEST way?
questions.explain: Key: B. Find and Replace searches for every occurrence of ‘Phillipsburg’ and replaces it with ‘Philipsburg’ in one operation.

questions.stem: Which text wrapping option allows a paragraph to flow closely around the OUTLINE of an irregularly shaped logo?
questions.explain: Key: D. Tight wrapping makes the text follow the outline of the graphic itself rather than a rectangular box around it.

questions.stem: A school is setting up a database table of its students. Which field is MOST suitable as the primary key?
questions.explain: Key: C. A primary key must uniquely identify each record. Two students may share a surname, birthday or form class, but each has a different ID number.

questions.stem: A database object used to extract ONLY those records that meet stated criteria, such as all customers who live in Holetown, is a
questions.explain: Key: C. A query retrieves the subset of records that match given criteria. A form is for entering data and a report presents it.

questions.stem: Which presentation feature allows a change to the font and logo on EVERY slide to be made in one place?
questions.explain: Key: D. Editing the slide master applies the design change to all slides based on it at once.

questions.stem: In a semi-blocked letter, which of the following parts are normally positioned towards the RIGHT of the page?
options: The date and the complimentary close
The reference and the inside address
The subject heading and the enclosure notation
The inside address and the salutation
questions.explain: Key: A. A semi-blocked letter keeps its paragraphs at the left margin like a blocked letter, but the date and the closing are indented towards the right.

questions.stem:
Which of the following should appear in the continuation heading at the top of the second page of a two-page business letter?

I. The recipient's name
II. The page number
III. The date
IV. The sender's telephone number
questions.explain: Key: C. A continuation heading shows the recipient's name, the page number and the date. The sender's telephone number is already in the letterhead on page 1.

questions.stem: A letter to the Human Resources Manager gives details of an employee's medical leave and should be opened ONLY by the addressee. Which special notation should be typed on the envelope?
questions.explain: Key: C. CONFIDENTIAL shows that the contents are sensitive and must be opened only by the named addressee. URGENT only signals that prompt action is needed.

questions.stem: A document in which a landlord in Grand Anse allows a tenant to occupy an apartment for 12 months in return for monthly rent is BEST described as a
questions.explain: Key: C. A lease sets out the terms on which the lessor allows the lessee to use property for a stated period, usually for rent. A conveyance transfers ownership.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT normally included in a memorandum?
questions.explain: Key: A. A memo is internal, so it opens with TO, FROM, DATE and SUBJECT headings and does not need an inside address.

questions.stem: Mrs Brooks wants to e-mail a price list to 35 customers who do not know one another, without any customer seeing the other addresses. In which field should she enter the customers' addresses?
questions.explain: Key: A. Addresses in the Bcc (blind carbon copy) field are hidden from the other recipients, which protects the customers' privacy.

questions.stem: A handwritten timesheet that a worker completes before the hours are keyed into the payroll system is an example of a
questions.explain: Key: C. A source document is the original document on which data is first recorded before it is entered into a data processing system.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are machine-readable documents?

I. A barcoded product label
II. An OMR answer sheet
III. A handwritten letter of complaint
IV. A QR code on a flyer
questions.explain: Key: D. Barcodes, OMR sheets and QR codes can be read directly by a scanning device. A handwritten letter must be keyed in by a person.

In the file path shown, ‘Term1’ represents
questions.explain: Key: D. ‘Term1’ is a folder nested inside the ‘EDPM’ folder, so it is a sub-folder. ‘C:’ is the drive and ‘.docx’ shows the file type.

questions.stem: Which of the following file names follows good practice AND will sort correctly by date?
questions.explain: Key: D. A name that starts with the date in YYYY-MM-DD form and then describes the content is clear and sorts in date order.

questions.stem: The accounts office at a St. George’s hardware store wants sales staff to be able to open the price list, but never to save any changes to it. Which file integrity measure is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Key: D. Read-only access lets users view a file's content but prevents them from saving changes to it.

questions.stem: Gros Islet Tours backs up its files every evening to an external hard drive kept on the shelf beside the office server. Why is this arrangement still risky?
options: Backups are only valid when they are printed
Fire or flooding in the office could destroy both copies
External hard drives cannot store spreadsheets
The backup is made too often to be useful
questions.explain: Key: B. Because the backup is kept in the same place as the original, a single physical disaster could destroy both. A copy should also be kept off-site or in the cloud.

questions.stem: Moving completed files that are rarely used out of active storage and into organised long-term storage is called
questions.explain: Key: B. Archiving keeps older records for future reference while keeping active storage efficient. Disposal destroys records.

questions.stem: Information such as the date a file was created, the date it was last modified and the name of its owner is known as
questions.explain: Key: A. Metadata is data about a file, rather than its content, and it helps trace who created or changed a document and when.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are CYBER security measures for protecting files?

I. A firewall
II. Strong passwords
III. A fireproof cabinet
IV. Encryption
questions.explain: Key: C. Firewalls, passwords and encryption protect digital files from unauthorised access. A fireproof cabinet is a physical security measure.

questions.stem: Copying paragraphs from a website into an SBA report without quotation marks or a citation is an example of
questions.explain: Key: B. Plagiarism is using another person's words or ideas without giving them appropriate credit.

questions.stem: Danielle hands in an essay she wrote for another subject last year as her new assignment, without telling her teacher. This is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: C. Reusing one's own earlier work as if it were new, without acknowledging it, is self-plagiarism.

questions.stem: A magazine pays a Grand Anse photographer to use her picture of Gouyave, but then alters the colours and crops out her signature without her consent. Which of the photographer's rights has been violated?
questions.explain: Key: A. She was paid, so her economic rights were respected; altering the work without consent harms its integrity, which breaches her moral rights.

questions.stem: The brand name and logo used to identify a company's products are protected as a
questions.explain: Key: B. Trademarks protect symbols, names and logos that identify a business or its products. Patents protect inventions.

questions.stem: Mr Lake finds a diagram released under a Creative Commons licence that allows reuse with attribution. What must he do to use it ethically in his class handout?
options: Remove the creator's name and add his own
Pay a royalty to the website before using it
Use it without credit because it is free
Use it and credit the creator as the licence requires
questions.explain: Key: D. A Creative Commons attribution licence allows free reuse provided the creator is credited in the way the licence states.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are examples of good netiquette?

I. Typing the whole message in capital letters
II. Checking the recipients before pressing Send
III. Forwarding a colleague's private e-mail without permission
IV. Using a clear, specific subject line
questions.explain: Key: B. Checking recipients and writing a clear subject line are courteous practices. Typing in capitals reads as shouting, and forwarding private mail without permission breaches trust.

questions.stem: Jerome files all the invoices correctly and on time even when his supervisor is away from the office. Which work attitude does this show?
questions.explain: Key: D. Completing tasks reliably and to standard without anyone watching shows individual responsibility (working without supervision).

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST way for a student to make sure an assignment meets acceptable standards and is handed in on time?
options: Ask a friend to complete the difficult parts
Submit the first draft without proofreading it
Plan the tasks, set interim deadlines and leave time to proofread
Begin the work on the night before the deadline
questions.explain: Key: C. Effective time management, with planned stages and time left for review, lets work be checked and submitted by the deadline.

questions.stem: During a virtual staff meeting, which of the following behaviours shows appropriate remote working etiquette?
options: Joining fifteen minutes late without notice
Muting the microphone when not speaking
Eating a meal with the camera switched on
Replying to personal text messages during the meeting
questions.explain: Key: B. Muting when not speaking cuts background noise and shows courtesy to other participants; the other behaviours are unprofessional.

questions.stem:

questions.explain: Key: A. Days of the week are proper nouns and must begin with a capital letter: “Monday”.

Please bring the following items; a pen, a calculator and your student ID card.
questions.explain: Key: C. A list that follows a complete introductory statement is introduced by a colon, not a semicolon: “items:”.

Ms Richardson asked whether the monthly reports had been printed.
questions.explain: Key: B. This is an indirect (reported) question, so it correctly ends with a full stop, not a question mark.

questions.stem: The new filing policy will ……… every department in the school.
questions.explain: Key: D. “Affect” is the verb meaning “to have an influence on”; “effect” is normally a noun.

questions.stem: All visitors must report to the reception desk on ……… at the Bayside Medical Centre.
questions.explain: Key: B. The correct spelling is “arrival” — double r, single l.

questions.stem: Each member of staff must keep ……… password private.
questions.explain: Key: B. “Their” is the possessive form; “they’re” means “they are” and “there” refers to a place.

questions.stem: The committee could not reach a decision because the members ……… on the date of the next meeting.
questions.explain: Key: D. The sentence is in the past tense (“could not reach”), so the past tense “disagreed” is required.

questions.stem: The office manager ordered new letterheads, envelopes and other ……… for the front desk.
questions.explain: Key: C. “Stationery” (with -ery) means writing materials; “stationary” means not moving.

questions.stem: Please find ……… a copy of the signed lease agreement.
questions.explain: Key: D. The accepted business phrase is “Please find enclosed”, using the past participle.

questions.stem: The new database will make it easier for staff to ……… customer records quickly.
questions.explain: Key: C. “Retrieve” follows the rule “i before e except after c”.

questions.stem: Which of the following words is represented by the abbreviation ‘accom’ in a manuscript?
questions.explain: Key: B. ‘accom’ is the standard manuscript abbreviation for “accommodation” and must be typed in full.

questions.stem: A typist sees the correction sign ‘stet’ written in the margin beside a word that has been crossed out and has a dotted line beneath it. What should the typist do?
options: Transpose the word with the word next to it
Leave the word as it was originally written
Delete the word and close up the space
Spell the word out in full
questions.explain: Key: B. ‘Stet’ means “let it stand” — ignore the correction and keep the original text.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices is used for BOTH input and output?
questions.explain: Key: A. A touchscreen displays output and accepts input through the same surface; the others are input only or output only.

questions.stem: A receptionist at a hotel in Gros Islet places her finger on a reader to clock in at the start of each shift. This device is BEST described as a(n)
questions.explain: Key: D. A biometric device reads a unique physical characteristic, such as a fingerprint, to identify the user.

questions.stem: Which storage medium would BEST allow staff at the Bridgetown and Holetown branches of a company to open and edit the same files from different locations?
questions.explain: Key: B. Cloud storage is accessed over the internet, so files can be saved, synced and shared from any location.

questions.stem: Software that coordinates the activities among a computer’s hardware devices and allows the user to run application software is called
questions.explain: Key: B. The operating system manages memory, devices and processing, and provides the platform on which applications run.

questions.stem: Which of the following practices will MOST help to reduce eye strain for a data entry clerk who works at a monitor all day?
options: Raising the height of the chair
Taking regular breaks to look away from the screen
questions.explain: Key: C. Regular breaks that rest the eyes from the screen reduce eye strain; the other options deal with posture or convenience.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are SAFETY practices in a computer laboratory?
I. Avoid overloading electrical outlets.
II. Keep cables away from walkways.
III. Adjust the brightness of the monitor.
questions.explain: Key: A. I and II prevent fires, shocks and trips; III is a health (eye comfort) measure rather than a safety practice.

questions.stem: Before disconnecting a flash drive from a computer, a user should FIRST
questions.explain: Key: A. Safely removing (ejecting) external storage prevents data loss or file corruption.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices would allow a blind employee to read text displayed on the screen?
questions.explain: Key: B. A Braille display converts on-screen text into raised Braille characters.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT · Kemal is a clerk at a law office on Broad Street. His monitor is placed on top of a stack of files so that the screen is above his eye level. The screen faces a large window and he often sees glare. His keyboard is at elbow height and his chair has an adjustable back rest.

Which of the following changes would improve the ergonomics of Kemal’s workstation?
I. Lower the monitor so that the top of the screen is at or slightly below eye level.
II. Turn the monitor so that it no longer faces the window.
III. Raise the keyboard so that it is well above elbow height.
questions.explain: Key: C. Lowering the monitor and reducing glare correct the two problems; a keyboard well above elbow height would strain the wrists and shoulders.

questions.stem: Which type of application software is MOST suitable for recording a term’s attendance and calculating each student’s percentage attendance?
questions.explain: Key: B. Spreadsheets organise numerical data in rows and columns and perform calculations automatically.

questions.explain: Key: B. Conditional formatting automatically changes the appearance of cells that meet a stated condition.

questions.explain: Key: D. The condition must be C2>=50 so that a mark of exactly 50 also passes, followed by the value if true and the value if false.

questions.explain: Key: B. Telephone numbers contain symbols and spaces and are never calculated, so they are stored as Text.

questions.explain: Key: C. Queries and reports (with tables and forms) are database objects; a slide belongs to presentation software.

questions.stem: Which feature of presentation software controls the visual effect seen as the show moves from one slide to the next?
questions.explain: Key: D. A transition is applied between slides; animation applies to objects within a slide.

questions.stem: A secretary wants to combine a standard letter with a list of 200 names and addresses stored in a database to produce personalised letters. Which feature should she use?
questions.explain: Key: B. Mail merge combines a main document with a data source to generate many personalised copies.

questions.stem: In which letter style does every line, including the date and the complimentary close, begin at the left margin?
questions.explain: Key: D. In the blocked style every line starts at the left margin with no indentation.

questions.stem: Which envelope size is designed to hold an A4 sheet folded into thirds?

questions.stem: Which meeting document is prepared for the chairperson only and contains extra notes beside each item to be discussed?
questions.explain: Key: D. A chairman’s agenda is an expanded agenda with space and notes for the chairperson’s use.

questions.stem: Which legal document sets out the terms under which one party allows another to use a property for a stated period, usually in exchange for rent?
questions.explain: Key: A. A lease is an agreement between a lessor and a lessee for the use of property for a period of time.

questions.stem: The manager of a hardware store in Portsmouth wants the sales chart in her monthly report to update automatically whenever the spreadsheet figures change. Which type of graph should be inserted into the report?
options: Hand-drawn graph scanned into the report
Picture of the graph pasted from the clipboard
questions.explain: Key: A. A linked graph stays connected to its source data and updates when the data changes; an embedded graph is a fixed snapshot.

questions.stem: The events coordinator of a Gros Islet resort needs to e-mail the same announcement to 60 guests who do not know one another, without revealing their e-mail addresses. Which field should she use for the guests’ addresses?
questions.explain: Key: B. Bcc (blind carbon copy) hides recipients’ addresses from one another.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are DISADVANTAGES of electronic communication?
I. A wrong attachment can be sent by mistake.
II. A message may be filtered into a spam folder and not seen.
III. One message can be sent to many recipients at the same time.
questions.explain: Key: A. Errors in dispatch (I) and uncertainty that a message is received (II) are disadvantages; sending to many recipients at once (III) is an advantage.

questions.stem: A secretary needs to locate every e-mail exchanged with one particular supplier over the past year. Which method of sorting the mailbox would be MOST useful?
questions.explain: Key: A. Sorting by sender groups together all messages from one person or organisation.

questions.stem: A completed order form on which a customer’s purchase details are FIRST written is an example of a
questions.explain: Key: A. A source document is the original document on which data is first recorded before it is processed.

questions.stem: A water bill with a payment stub that the customer tears off and returns with payment is BEST described as a
questions.explain: Key: A. A turnaround document is produced by a system, sent out, and returned as input for further processing.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT · File path on a company computer:

D:\Front Office\2026\Invoices\INV-0417.docx
In the file path shown in the exhibit, which item is a SUB-FOLDER?
questions.explain: Key: D. D: is the drive, Front Office is the main folder on that drive, 2026 is a sub-folder inside it, and INV-0417.docx is the file.

questions.stem: A company wants all staff to be able to VIEW the staff handbook, but not to change it by accident. Which file integrity measure is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Key: D. Read-only access lets users open and view a file but prevents them from saving changes.

questions.stem: Converting the content of a file into a coded form that can only be read by someone with the correct key or password is called
questions.explain: Key: B. Encryption protects content even if the file itself is accessed without authorisation.

questions.stem:
Which of the following would protect a small business in Gros Islet from losing its files if its office were damaged by a hurricane?
I. Keeping a backup copy at an off-site location
II. Saving backup copies to cloud storage
III. Keeping a second hard drive on a shelf in the same office
questions.explain: Key: B. Off-site and cloud backups survive damage to the premises; a backup kept in the same office would be destroyed with the originals.

questions.stem: The length of time a document must be kept, as set by organisational policy or by law, is known as its
questions.explain: Key: C. The retention period is how long a record must be kept before it may be archived or disposed of.

Created3 March 2026
Modified12 March 2026
Accessed15 March 2026
Owneraccounts01
According to the file properties shown, on which date was the CONTENT of the file last changed?
questions.explain: Key: C. The “Modified” date records when the content was last changed; “Accessed” only shows when the file was last opened.

questions.stem: Which of the following file names follows good practice so that files sort correctly by date?
questions.explain: Key: B. Placing the date first in YYYY-MM-DD format with a clear descriptive name makes files sort in date order.

questions.stem: A singer receives a fee each time a radio station plays her song. This payment is an example of the singer’s
questions.explain: Key: A. Economic rights entitle a creator to be paid, for example through royalties, when others use the work.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT · A newspaper in Roseau paid a photographer the agreed fee to print one of her photographs and credited her by name. However, the editor altered the photograph without her consent, changing its meaning in a way that damaged her reputation.

Which of the photographer’s rights has the newspaper violated?
questions.explain: Key: C. She was paid, so her economic rights were respected, but altering the work without consent breaches her moral rights.

questions.stem: Jada submitted an essay she had written last year for another subject as a new assignment, without telling her teacher. This act is called
questions.explain: Key: C. Self-plagiarism is reusing one’s own earlier work without acknowledging that it has been used before.

questions.stem:
Which of the following practices help a student to AVOID plagiarism?
I. Including in-text citations for sources used
II. Changing a few words in a copied paragraph
III. Providing a bibliography at the end of the document
questions.explain: Key: B. Citations and a bibliography acknowledge sources; changing only a few words of copied text is still plagiarism.

questions.stem: Teaching and learning materials that are deliberately released for free use, adaptation and sharing by the public are called
questions.explain: Key: C. Open Educational Resources (OERs) are released for free use, often under Creative Commons licences.

questions.stem: Typing an entire e-mail message in capital letters is considered poor netiquette because it
options: is always blocked by spam filters
questions.explain: Key: D. Text written entirely in capitals is widely read as shouting and appears rude.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT · Darnell is an office assistant at a firm on Frederick Street. While his supervisor was overseas for a week, he completed all of his filing and data entry accurately and on time without being reminded.

Which desirable work attitude is shown by Darnell in the extract?
questions.explain: Key: D. Completing tasks reliably and to standard without supervision shows individual responsibility.

questions.stem: Repeated, deliberate harm directed at another person through online messages and posts is called
questions.explain: Key: D. Cyberbullying is repeated, deliberate harm aimed at someone online and is a serious breach of netiquette.

questions.stem: After e-mailing an important contract to a client, Ms Hodge telephones the client the next day to confirm that it was received. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: C. Follow-up procedures involve checking that work sent or delegated was received and acted upon.

questions.stem:
Items 1–3. Each sentence below may contain an error of punctuation or capitalisation. Select the letter (A), (B) or (C) that identifies the underlined part containing the error. Select (D) if there is NO ERROR.

The committee will meet on monday, 9 March (A) at the Basseterre Community Centre (B) at 4:00 p.m. (C)
questions.explain: Key: A. Days of the week are proper nouns and always take a capital letter, so “monday” must be typed “Monday”.

questions.stem:
Items 1–3. Each sentence below may contain an error of punctuation or capitalisation. Select the letter (A), (B) or (C) that identifies the underlined part containing the error. Select (D) if there is NO ERROR.

“Please file these invoices,” (A) said Mrs Arrindell, (B) “before you leave.” (C)
questions.explain: Key: D. The interrupted quotation is punctuated correctly: a comma inside the first closing quotation mark, a comma after the speaker tag, and the second part starts with a small letter because it continues the same sentence.

questions.stem:
Items 1–3. Each sentence below may contain an error of punctuation or capitalisation. Select the letter (A), (B) or (C) that identifies the underlined part containing the error. Select (D) if there is NO ERROR.

The students’ (A) projects were displayed in the library; (B) and the principal (C) praised every one of them.
questions.explain: Key: B. A semicolon is not used before a joining word such as “and”; a comma (or no mark) is needed. “students’” is a correct plural possessive and “principal” needs no capital when not followed by a name.

questions.stem: The new adjustable chairs have had a positive ……… on the comfort of the office staff.
questions.explain: Key: B. “Effect” is the noun meaning a result; “affect” is normally a verb. The other two options are misspellings.

questions.stem: The secretary booked ……… at a Montego Bay hotel for the visiting auditors.
questions.explain: Key: B. “Accommodation” is spelt with a double c and a double m.

questions.stem: Neither the manager nor the clerks ……… aware of the change in the filing procedure.
questions.explain: Key: C. With “neither … nor”, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. “Clerks” is plural and the sentence is in the past tense, so “were” is correct.

questions.stem: The office ……… cupboard was restocked with letterheads, envelopes and file folders.
questions.explain: Key: D. “Stationery” (with -ery) means writing and office materials; “stationary” means not moving.

questions.stem: By the time the auditors arrived, the accounts clerk ……… all the receipts in date order.
questions.explain: Key: B. The past perfect “had filed” shows an action completed before another past action (the auditors arrived).

questions.stem: Before printing, the typist must proofread the letter to make sure that it is ……… .
questions.explain: Key: D. “Mailable” (fit to be sent without further correction) is the correct spelling.

questions.stem: The hotel ……… the conference booking by e-mail within an hour of the request.
questions.explain: Key: C. To “confirm” is to state that something is definitely arranged. The other words look similar but mean to comply, to restrict and to grant or discuss.

questions.stem: In a manuscript, the abbreviation ‘approx’ should be typed in full as
questions.explain: Key: C. ‘approx’ is the accepted short form of ‘approximately’ and is expanded in a formal typescript.

questions.stem: In a manuscript, words have been crossed out, a row of dots has been placed beneath them and the word ‘stet’ is written in the margin. The typist should
options: retain the crossed-out words as originally written
move the crossed-out words to the end of the sentence
type the crossed-out words in bold
questions.explain: Key: A. ‘Stet’ means “let it stand”: ignore the correction and keep the original words.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices is used by banks to read the special characters printed at the bottom of cheques?
questions.explain: Key: D. Magnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR) reads the magnetic-ink numbers on cheques.

questions.stem: A touch screen used at a self check-in kiosk at V.C. Bird International Airport is BEST described as
options: both an input and an output device
questions.explain: Key: A. The screen displays information (output) and accepts the passenger’s touches (input), so it is an input/output device.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are examples of secondary (backing) storage?
I. Flash drive
II. RAM
III. External hard drive
IV. Cloud storage
questions.explain: Key: B. RAM is primary (main) memory and is volatile; flash drives, external hard drives and cloud storage keep data permanently and are secondary storage.

questions.stem: Which type of software manages the computer’s resources, controls its hardware and provides the user interface?
questions.explain: Key: A. The operating system is system software that manages hardware, memory and files and lets the user interact with the computer.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT

Keisha is a data-entry clerk at an insurance office in Couva. She types for about six hours each day with her wrists bent upward and resting on the hard edge of the desk. By the end of each day her wrists and fingers ache.

Which of the following actions would BEST reduce Keisha’s discomfort?
options: Using a wrist rest and keeping her wrists straight
Placing the monitor slightly below eye level
Increasing the font size on her monitor
questions.explain: Key: A. Bent, unsupported wrists during long periods of typing lead to repetitive strain injury; a wrist rest and a straight (neutral) wrist position reduce the strain. The other options address the eyes or neck.

questions.stem: Eye strain caused by long periods of looking at a computer screen can BEST be reduced by
options: taking regular short breaks to rest the eyes
questions.explain: Key: C. Regular breaks (looking away from the screen) relax the eye muscles. Keyboards and footrests help other parts of the body, and sitting closer makes eye strain worse.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are SAFETY practices in a computer laboratory?
I. Keeping cables tidy and away from walkways
II. Connecting equipment through a surge protector
III. Adjusting the height of the chair
questions.explain: Key: B. Tidy cables prevent trips and falls, and surge protectors prevent electrical damage and fire. Adjusting chair height is an ergonomic (comfort and posture) practice.

questions.stem: Before removing a flash drive from a computer, a user should FIRST
questions.explain: Key: B. Ejecting the device safely makes sure all data has finished writing, which avoids file loss or corruption.

questions.stem: Which of the following practices BEST reduces the environmental impact of a busy office?
options: Recycling used paper and toner cartridges
Printing every e-mail for the files
questions.explain: Key: A. Recycling reduces waste sent to landfill. The other practices waste paper, electricity or equipment.

questions.stem: Which type of application software would be MOST suitable for designing a new logo for San Pedro Marine Supplies Ltd?
questions.explain: Key: A. Graphic software is used to create and edit images, illustrations and design elements such as logos.

questions.stem: Which word processing feature should be used to produce a personalised letter for each of 80 customers whose names and addresses are stored in a spreadsheet?
questions.explain: Key: B. Mail merge combines a main document with a data source to produce one personalised copy for every record.

questions.stem:

questions.stem: A clerk enters =B2+C2+D2 in cell E2 and copies it down to E5. Each new cell correctly adds the figures in its own row because the formula uses
questions.explain: Key: A. Relative references change automatically when a formula is copied, so the formula becomes =B3+C3+D3 in E3, and so on.

questions.stem: In a database of guests at a Grand Anse hotel, the complete set of details about ONE guest (name, room number and arrival date) is called a
questions.explain: Key: C. A record holds all the fields about one person or item. A field is a single item of data, such as the room number.

questions.stem: Which field would be MOST suitable as the primary key in a table of employees?
questions.explain: Key: B. A primary key must be unique for every record. Two employees may share a last name, department or date of birth, but each has a different employee ID.

questions.stem: In presentation software, the pre-set arrangements of placeholders for a title, text and pictures on a slide are called
questions.explain: Key: C. Layouts arrange title, content and image placeholders so information is organised consistently from slide to slide.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT

Mr Richardson is preparing a slide show for the Bayleaf Hill Secondary School Parents’ Evening. He wants the school crest and the footer text to appear in exactly the same position on every slide, and he wants to be able to change the font on all twelve slides in one step.

Which feature should Mr Richardson use?
questions.explain: Key: A. Editing the slide master applies a design, logo, footer and fonts to every slide at once, and a change made there updates the whole presentation.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about transitions and animations in a business presentation are TRUE?
I. They should be applied consistently.
II. They should be added to every bullet point to keep the audience alert.
III. They should support, not distract from, the message.
questions.explain: Key: B. Transitions and animations should be consistent and used sparingly so that they support the speaker. Animating every bullet point overuses them and distracts the audience.

questions.stem: While designing a flyer, Lena combined a photograph, a text box and a background rectangle so that they can be moved and resized as ONE object. Which feature did she use?
questions.explain: Key: D. Grouping joins separate objects into a single unit; ungrouping separates them again so each can be edited.

questions.stem: A company logo must stay sharp whether it is printed on a business card or on a large billboard. The logo should therefore be created as a
questions.explain: Key: D. Vector graphics are built from mathematical paths and can be resized to any size without losing quality. Raster (bitmap) images, including JPEGs, become blurred when enlarged.

questions.stem: Which meeting document is prepared for the person presiding ONLY and contains extra notes and background information beside each item?
questions.explain: Key: B. The chairman’s agenda is an expanded agenda for the chairperson, with space or notes beside each item to guide the meeting.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT

GOUYAVE YOUTH CLUB
Monthly Meeting · Thursday, 14 May 2026 · 6:30 p.m.
AGENDA

  1. Apologies for absence
  2. Minutes of the last meeting
  3. ………………………
  4. Correspondence
  5. Treasurer’s report
  6. Any other business
  7. Date of next meeting
Which item is MISSING at number 3 of the agenda?
questions.explain: Key: D. “Matters arising” (from the minutes) normally follows immediately after the minutes of the last meeting have been read and confirmed.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT

A letter from Montego Bay Realty Ltd has the date, inside address, salutation, every paragraph, the complimentary close and the signature block all starting at the left margin. A blank line separates each paragraph.

In which style has the letter been displayed?
questions.explain: Key: B. In the blocked (fully blocked) style every line begins at the left margin. Semi-blocked letters indent the date and closing; indented letters also indent the paragraphs.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are NOT normally included in a memorandum?
I. Salutation
II. Subject heading
III. Complimentary close
IV. Date
questions.explain: Key: B. A memo opens with a TO/FROM/DATE/SUBJECT heading block and does not need a salutation (Dear …) or a complimentary close (Yours …).

questions.stem: A DL envelope is designed to hold an A4 letter that has been folded
questions.explain: Key: B. The DL envelope (11 cm × 22 cm) takes an A4 sheet folded into thirds; a C5 envelope takes A4 folded in half.

questions.stem: In a lease, the person who owns the property and allows another person to use it in exchange for rent is called the
questions.explain: Key: D. The lessor grants the lease; the lessee (tenant) pays rent to use the property.

questions.explain: Key: D. 19.50 + 96.00 + 15.00 = US$130.50. US$58.25 is the sum of the unit prices only.

questions.stem: The secretary of the Holetown Community Council wants to e-mail the minutes to 30 residents without allowing the residents to see one another’s e-mail addresses. She should enter the addresses in the
questions.explain: Key: C. Blind carbon copy (Bcc) sends the message without showing those addresses to the other recipients.

questions.stem: An office administrator needs to find every e-mail received from one supplier over the past year. Which method of organising the inbox would be MOST useful?
questions.explain: Key: B. Sorting by sender groups together all messages from the same person or organisation.

questions.stem: An electricity bill sent to a customer, part of which is returned with the payment for further processing, is an example of a
questions.explain: Key: D. A turnaround document is produced by a system, sent out, and returned as input for further processing.

questions.stem:

D:\School\Business Dept\EDPM\Term 1\Lesson_Notes_Week3.docx
In the file path shown, ‘Term 1’ is a
questions.explain: Key: B. D: is the drive, School is a folder, and Business Dept, EDPM and Term 1 are sub-folders nested inside it. Lesson_Notes_Week3 is the file and .docx is its extension.

questions.stem: Which of the following file names follows good practice for an electronic filing system?
questions.explain: Key: D. Good file names are clear, descriptive and consistent; a date in YYYY-MM-DD format also makes files sort correctly by date.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT

The Human Resources office of a hotel in San Pedro places the staff handbook on a shared drive. All staff must be able to open and read the handbook, but no one except the Human Resources manager should be able to change it.

Which file integrity measure is MOST appropriate for the staff handbook?
questions.explain: Key: C. Read-only access lets users view a file but prevents them from making or saving changes.

questions.stem: A small business in San Pedro backs up all its files to a second hard drive kept on the same desk as the main computer. What is the GREATEST weakness of this arrangement?
options: Files cannot be restored from a hard drive
The second drive will make all files read-only
The backups will take too long to complete
One fire or flood could destroy both copies at once
questions.explain: Key: D. A backup kept in the same place as the original is exposed to the same physical disaster; at least one copy should be kept off-site or in the cloud.

questions.stem:
Which of the following are CYBER security measures?
I. Firewall
II. Fireproof filing cabinet
III. Strong passwords
IV. Encryption
questions.explain: Key: C. Firewalls, passwords and encryption protect data electronically. A fireproof cabinet is a physical security measure.

questions.stem: The length of time a document must be kept before it may be securely disposed of is called its
questions.explain: Key: D. The retention period is set by organisational policy or by law; after it ends the file may be destroyed or deleted securely.

questions.stem:

According to the metadata shown, on which date was the CONTENT of the report last changed?
questions.explain: Key: C. “Date modified” records the last change to the content. “Date accessed” (16 March) only shows when the file was last opened.

questions.stem: Which practice would allow an office to restore a shared report to the way it looked before an incorrect figure was entered last week?
questions.explain: Key: C. Versioning keeps successive saved versions of a document, so an earlier version can be reviewed, compared or restored.

questions.stem: Which right allows a St. Lucian songwriter to receive royalties when a radio station broadcasts her song?
questions.explain: Key: B. Economic rights entitle the creator to payment, such as royalties or licence fees, when others use the work.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT

A St. George’s magazine paid photographer Arlene the agreed fee to print her photograph of Grand Anse. Without asking her, the editor changed the colours, cut away part of the image and printed it under another photographer’s name.

Which of Arlene’s rights has been MOST clearly infringed?
questions.explain: Key: C. Arlene was paid, so her economic rights were respected. Altering her work without consent and removing her name damage its integrity and her reputation, which are moral rights.

questions.stem: For his EDPM research paper, Devon submitted an essay he had written for Business Studies the previous year, without telling his teacher. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: C. Reusing one’s own earlier work without acknowledging that it has been used before is self-plagiarism.

questions.stem:
Which of the following practices help a student to avoid plagiarism?
I. Using in-text citations
II. Including a bibliography
III. Changing a few words in a copied paragraph
IV. Obtaining permission to use another person’s photograph
questions.explain: Key: B. Citations, a bibliography and permission all credit the original creator. Changing only a few words of copied text is still plagiarism.

questions.stem: A teacher finds a diagram released under a Creative Commons licence that allows sharing with attribution. Before using it in a class handout, she must
options: remove the creator’s name to keep the handout tidy
credit the creator in the way the licence requires
pay the creator a royalty for each copy
register the diagram as her own work
questions.explain: Key: B. An attribution licence allows free use as long as the creator is credited as the licence specifies.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of GOOD netiquette when writing a business e-mail?
options: Typing the whole message in capital letters
Reviewing the tone and the recipients before sending
Replying to all recipients with personal comments
Forwarding a colleague’s private message without permission
questions.explain: Key: B. “Think and check before sending” is a basic rule of netiquette. Capital letters read as shouting, and sharing private messages or personal remarks is discourteous.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT

“Sharon completes her filing accurately and on time, even on days when her supervisor is away at the Grand Anse branch.”

Which desirable work attitude is described in the extract?
questions.explain: Key: C. Completing tasks reliably and to standard when no one is checking shows individual responsibility, or the ability to work without supervision.

questions.stem:
EXHIBIT

At 8:00 a.m. Jamal, an office assistant, has three tasks:

  1. Type the minutes of yesterday’s board meeting, due to the chairman at 10:00 a.m. today.
  2. File last year’s correspondence in the archive room.
  3. Design a flyer for a fundraising event next month.
Which of the following approaches shows the BEST time management?
options: File the correspondence first because it is the easiest task
Design the flyer first because it is the most creative task
Type the minutes first because they are due earliest
Work on all three tasks at the same time
questions.explain: Key: C. Effective time management means prioritising by deadline and importance; the minutes are needed within two hours, so they come first.

questions.stem: Two days after e-mailing a quotation to a client in Bathsheba, Mrs Lake telephones the client to confirm that it was received. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: D. Follow-up procedures involve checking that work sent or delegated has been received and acted upon.

questions.stem: A computer is BEST described as a(n)
options: type of software used to browse the internet
mechanical device that stores paper records
electronic machine that accepts and processes data to produce information
questions.explain: The syllabus defines a computer as an electronic machine or device that accepts and processes data to produce information. Option D is tempting because computers do accept input, but a computer also processes data and produces output; a peripheral is only one part of the system.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the CORRECT order of the computing cycle?
questions.explain: Data must first be input, then processed, then presented as output, and then stored for later use. Option B is tempting because processing is the "work" of the computer, but nothing can be processed until data has been input.

questions.stem: At a supermarket till, the total amount due shown on the display is an example of
questions.explain: The prices have been processed (added, with tax calculated) into a meaningful result, so the total is information. Option D is tempting because the total is made of numbers, but data refers to raw facts before processing.

questions.stem: Which category of computer is generally used to support hundreds or thousands of users at the same time?
questions.explain: Mainframes are large, powerful computers used by banks, airlines and governments to support hundreds or thousands of simultaneous users. Option B is tempting because minicomputers also serve several users, but only tens to hundreds, not thousands.

questions.stem: A microcomputer is so named because it is built around
questions.explain: A microcomputer is a small, relatively inexpensive computer built around a single microprocessor chip. Option A is tempting because many microcomputers are small, but desktops with large monitors are also microcomputers; the name refers to the microprocessor.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the main components of a computer system?
questions.explain: An internet service provider is an outside company that supplies internet access; it is not a component of the computer system. Option B is tempting because peripherals are optional extras, but the syllabus lists peripherals as a main component.

questions.stem: Which of the following lists contains ONLY hardware?
questions.explain: A graphics tablet, a memory chip and a printer are all physical, tangible parts. Option C is tempting because two of its items are hardware, but a spreadsheet program is software.

questions.stem: Digital media differ from analog media in that digital media
options: can only be used for video
questions.explain: Digital media store and transmit information as discrete values, usually 0s and 1s. Option C is tempting to some, but it is the opposite of the truth: digital files can be copied with far less loss of quality than analog media.

questions.stem: Which part of the computer interprets instructions and performs calculations and logical comparisons?
questions.explain: The CPU carries out the processes between input and output. Option C is tempting because a sound card also processes data, but only audio data; the CPU interprets all instructions and manages the flow of data.

questions.stem: A peripheral is BEST described as
options: the CPU, motherboard and main memory
any hardware device connected to a computer that is not part of its essential core
any program installed on the hard drive
questions.explain: Peripherals are devices such as printers and scanners that connect to the core but are not part of it. Option A is tempting because it names hardware, but those three items ARE the essential core, so they are not peripherals.

questions.stem: Which factor of computer usage relates MOST directly to a computer producing correct results only when given correct data and instructions?
questions.explain: This is the "garbage in, garbage out" principle, which belongs under accuracy. Option D is tempting only because e-commerce systems also depend on data, but the principle is about the correctness of results, which is accuracy.

questions.stem: An office worker receives an e-mail that appears to be from her bank, asking her to click a link and enter her password. This is an example of
questions.explain: Phishing tricks users into revealing passwords or personal details by posing as a trusted organisation. Option C is tempting because ransomware is also a cyber security threat, but ransomware locks files until payment is made; it does not ask for a password by e-mail.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a DISADVANTAGE of e-commerce for a small business in Basseterre?
options: Building customer trust without face-to-face interaction
Reducing the cost of a physical storefront
questions.explain: Building trust online is a challenge of e-commerce. Options C, A and D are all advantages; option A is tempting because "around the clock" sounds like extra work, but the chapter lists it as a benefit.

questions.stem: A biometric device is BEST described as a device that
options: projects an image onto a screen
reads a unique physical characteristic to confirm identity
questions.explain: Fingerprint, facial and iris scanners read a unique physical characteristic for secure authentication. Option A is tempting because biometric data must be stored somewhere, but storing files is not what makes a device biometric.

questions.stem: Which device would a graphic designer use to draw directly into the computer with a pen-like stylus on a pressure-sensitive surface?
questions.explain: A graphics tablet lets an artist or designer draw or trace using a stylus on a flat, pressure-sensitive surface. Option C is tempting because a scanner also brings images into the computer, but it converts existing printed images rather than letting the designer draw.

questions.stem: A video card is described as supporting output because it
options: displays images directly to the user
processes image data and generates the visual output sent to the monitor
questions.explain: The video card prepares the image signal; the monitor is the device that actually displays it. Option A is tempting, but that is the monitor's job, which is why the video card is not strictly an output device.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices functions as BOTH an input and an output device?
questions.explain: A touchscreen accepts taps (input) and displays information (output) through the same component. Option A is tempting because a scanner deals with images, but it only sends data into the computer, so it is input only.

questions.stem: A device that blends the features of a smartphone and a tablet, with a larger touchscreen than a typical phone, is called a
questions.explain: A phablet combines phone and tablet features. Option A is tempting because of the word "mini", but a minicomputer is a mid-sized multi-user computer, not a handheld device.

questions.stem: Which storage medium is considered legacy technology, having been largely replaced by flash drives and cloud storage?
questions.explain: Optical discs such as the CD-ROM are now legacy technology in most everyday settings. Option B is tempting because hard disks have been around a long time, but fixed and portable hard disks are still in everyday use.

questions.stem: Three students living in different districts must edit the same SBA document during the week. Which storage option is MOST suitable?
options: The fixed hard disk of one student's laptop
A memory card in a camera
questions.explain: Cloud storage allows files to be saved, synced and shared across devices from any location. Option A is tempting because a hard disk holds plenty of data, but the other two students could not reach it from their homes.

questions.stem: Operating system software is BEST described as programs that
options: coordinate activities among hardware devices and allow the user to run application software
perform specific tasks such as word processing
are always accessed through a web browser
questions.explain: This is the syllabus definition of operating system software (e.g. Windows, Android). Option B is tempting because it describes software too, but performing specific tasks for users is the definition of application software.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of web-based application software?
options: A word processor installed on a laptop's hard drive
An online collaborative document editor accessed through a browser
Anti-virus software installed on a desktop
questions.explain: Web-based software is not installed on the hard drive but is accessed via the web, often with collaboration tools. Option B is tempting because word processing can be done online, but this option says the program is installed, so it is computer-based.

questions.stem: Which type of application software would a school office use to store and retrieve the records of 900 students in a structured way?
questions.explain: Database management software stores, organises and retrieves large, structured collections of data. Option C is tempting only because presentations can display records, but presentation software is designed for slides, not for storing and searching data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a recommended way of caring for peripherals?
options: Removing a flash drive at any time without warning
Keeping drinks beside the keyboard for convenience
Safely ejecting external storage devices before disconnecting them
Disabling the firewall for faster performance
questions.explain: Safely removing devices prevents data loss or corruption. Option D is tempting because some users believe it speeds things up, but turning off the firewall exposes the computer to unauthorised access, and it is not peripheral care.

questions.stem: Repetitive strain injury (RSI) is MOST closely linked to which factor associated with computer use?
questions.explain: RSI results from extended, uninterrupted use and poor workstation set-up, which ergonomics aims to prevent. Option A is tempting because it is also a factor of computer use, but environmental impact concerns energy and e-waste, not injury to the user.

questions.stem: On the home row, the left-hand fingers rest on which keys?
questions.explain: The left-hand fingers rest on A, S, D and F, with the index finger on the F bump. G, H, J, K is tempting because J has a bump too, but J belongs to the right hand, whose fingers rest on J, K, L and ;.

questions.stem: Which key allows a typist to switch between Insert mode and Overtype mode?
questions.explain: The Insert key toggles between Insert mode (new text pushes existing text forward) and Overtype mode (new text replaces it). Caps Lock is tempting because it also toggles a mode, but it only switches letters to uppercase.

questions.stem: The shortcut Ctrl + Z is used to
options: redo an action that was undone
questions.explain: Ctrl + Z undoes the most recent action. "Redo" is the most tempting distractor because it is closely related, but redo is Ctrl + Y.

questions.stem: In most word processing software, which function key starts a spelling and grammar check?
questions.explain: F7 starts the spelling and grammar check. F12 is tempting because it is also used in word processors, but it opens the Save As dialog box.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the correct position of the monitor for a typist?
options: Raised well above eye level so the typist sits upright
Top of the screen at or slightly below eye level, about arm's length away
As close to the face as possible so the text is easy to read
Flat on the desk below the keyboard
questions.explain: Correct screen-to-eye-level contact means the top of the screen is at or slightly below eye level, about arm's length away. Raising it well above eye level is tempting because it sounds like it improves posture, but it forces the head back and strains the neck.

questions.stem: A sit-stand workstation is BEST described as
options: a desk that can be raised or lowered so the user can alternate between sitting and standing
a keyboard split into two angled halves
a lamp designed to reduce screen glare
questions.explain: A sit-stand workstation is an adjustable desk that lets the user change position during the day. A chair with lumbar support is tempting because it is also an ergonomic trend, but it supports sitting only.

questions.stem: According to standard spacing rules, how many spaces should follow a comma?
questions.explain: There is no space before a comma and one space after it. Two is tempting because some older typewriting rules used two spaces after a full stop, but the rule in this course is one space after both.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correctly spaced?
options: The fair opens at 9:00 am; bring your cash box.
The fair opens at 9:00am; bring your cash box .
The fair opens at 9:00 am ;bring your cash box.
The fair opens at 9 : 00 am ; bring your cash box.
questions.explain: Times have no spaces round the colon, the semicolon has no space before and one after, and the full stop has no space before. Option B is tempting because the semicolon is right, but it has a space before the final full stop.

questions.stem: The manuscript sign "stet" instructs the typist to
questions.explain: Stet means "let it stand": ignore the correction and keep the original text. "Delete the marked word" is tempting because the word has been crossed out, but stet cancels that deletion.

questions.stem: The manuscript sign # means
questions.explain: The # sign means insert a space, used where two words have been run together. "Close up" is tempting because it also concerns spacing, but it means the opposite: remove unwanted space.

questions.stem: A typist sees "run on" in the margin beside the start of a paragraph. The typist should
options: indent the first line of the paragraph
join the paragraph to the end of the previous paragraph
start the paragraph on a new page
questions.explain: Run on (No ¶) means do not start a new paragraph; continue the text from the previous paragraph. Indenting is tempting, but an indent still starts a new paragraph.

questions.stem: In a manuscript, the words "also will" are marked with the sign Tr. The typist should type
questions.explain: Tr (transpose) means reverse the order of the marked words, so "also will" becomes "will also". Typing "also will" is tempting if you overlook the sign, but it leaves the error uncorrected.

questions.stem: When keying a formal letter from a manuscript, which of the following abbreviations should be typed in full?
questions.explain: "cttee" is writer's shorthand for "committee" and must be expanded. "e.g." is tempting because it is an abbreviation too, but it is an accepted abbreviation that may remain in a formal document.

questions.stem: The abbreviation "i.e." means
questions.explain: "i.e." means "that is" and introduces an exact explanation. "For example" is the most tempting distractor, but that is the meaning of "e.g.".

questions.stem: Which heading type is placed in the margin beside a block of text rather than within the line of text itself?
questions.explain: A marginal heading is a brief label in the left or right margin beside the text. A shoulder heading is tempting because it sits at the left margin, but it stands on its own line above the text, not beside it.

questions.stem: A heading that begins a paragraph, with the text of the paragraph continuing on the same line, is called a
questions.explain: A paragraph heading is followed by its text on the same line. A shoulder heading is tempting, but it stands on a line of its own.

questions.stem: In a hanging paragraph, which line begins at the left margin while the rest are indented?
questions.explain: In a hanging paragraph, the first line starts at the margin and all following lines are indented. "Every line" is tempting, but that describes a blocked paragraph.

questions.stem: An inset paragraph is MOST likely to be used to
options: start every paragraph in a business letter
set off a quotation from the surrounding text
show where a new page begins
questions.explain: An inset paragraph is indented from both margins to set off a quotation or example. A bibliography entry is tempting, but references use hanging paragraphs.

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences follows the accepted rules for typing figures?
options: Three groups of 12 students arrived at 9:00 am.
Three groups of 12 students arrived at nine am.
Three groups of twelve students arrived at 9:00 am.
3 groups of twelve students arrived at nine am.
questions.explain: Numbers one to nine are in words (three), 10 and above in numerals (12), and times are always numerals (9:00 am). Option B is tempting because the first two numbers are right, but times must be typed in numerals.

questions.stem: An ellipsis (...) is used to indicate that
options: an abbreviation should be spelled out
words have been intentionally omitted from a quoted passage
questions.explain: The ellipsis shows that words have been left out of a quotation, or that a thought trails off. "An abbreviation should be spelled out" is tempting because it also deals with shortening, but that instruction is the manuscript sign Sp.

questions.stem: Which of the following errors is a spelling and grammar checker LEAST likely to detect?
questions.explain: "Their" is a correctly spelled word, so the checker may not notice that it is the wrong word in context. The misspelling of a place name is tempting because checkers often mark local names, but a misspelling is still flagged as an unknown word.

questions.stem: What is the CSEC EDPM minimum typing speed benchmark?
options: 35 wpm with no error rate specified
questions.explain: The benchmark is a minimum of 35 wpm within a maximum 5 per cent error rate. The last option is tempting because the speed is right, but accuracy is part of the standard.

questions.stem: A typist produces 200 standard words in five minutes with 10 errors. What is the gross speed?
questions.explain: GWPM = 200 ÷ 5 = 40 wpm. 30 wpm is tempting if you subtract all 10 errors from 40, but gross speed is calculated before errors are taken into account.

questions.stem: Using the same figures (200 words, five minutes, 10 errors), what is the net speed?
questions.explain: NWPM = 40 − (10 ÷ 5) = 40 − 2 = 38 wpm. 30 wpm is tempting if you subtract all 10 errors, but the errors must first be divided by the number of minutes.

questions.stem: A student types 150 standard words in a three-minute test and makes 9 errors. Which of the following is correct?
options: The error rate is 6%, so the standard is not met even though the speed is 50 wpm.
The speed is below 35 wpm, so the standard is not met.
The error rate is 9%, so the standard is not met.
The error rate is 3%, so the standard is met.
questions.explain: GWPM = 150 ÷ 3 = 50 wpm, and the error rate = (9 ÷ 150) × 100 = 6%, which is above the 5% maximum. Option D is tempting if you divide errors by minutes (9 ÷ 3 = 3), but the error rate divides errors by WORDS.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes application software?
options: Programs designed to perform specific tasks for the user
Programs that coordinate the computer's hardware
Programs that only run inside a web browser
The physical parts of a computer system
questions.explain: Application software performs specific tasks for the user, such as producing a letter or a budget. Option B is tempting, but coordinating hardware is the job of operating system software, not application software.

questions.stem: Which type of application software is MOST suitable for storing and retrieving 5,000 structured customer records?
questions.explain: Large, structured collections of related records that must be retrieved efficiently call for database management software. A spreadsheet is the tempting distractor because it can hold a list, but it is not built for querying thousands of related records by combined conditions.

questions.stem: A file saved with the extension .xlsx was most likely created using
questions.explain: .xlsx is the Microsoft Excel workbook format. A word processor is tempting because .docx looks similar, but the "xls" letters identify Excel spreadsheets.

questions.stem: Google Docs is an example of
questions.explain: Google Docs runs inside a browser on remote servers and saves to the cloud, so it is web-based application software. "Computer-based" is tempting because Google Docs is a word processor like Word, but it is not installed on the hard drive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an ADVANCED feature of a word processor?
questions.explain: Mail merge combines a standard document with a data list to produce personalised copies, which is an advanced feature. Spelling check is tempting because it is automatic, but it is listed among the basic features.

questions.stem: The spreadsheet function used to add a range of values automatically is
questions.explain: SUM adds a range, e.g. =SUM(B2:B30). IF is tempting because it is also a common function, but IF tests a condition and returns one of two results; it does not add.

questions.stem: In a database, related data organised into rows and columns is BEST described as being stored in
questions.explain: A database stores related records (rows) and fields (columns) in tables. "A worksheet" is tempting because spreadsheets also use rows and columns, but a worksheet belongs to spreadsheet software, not a database.

questions.stem: Which presentation software feature allows a design to be applied and updated consistently across an entire slide deck at once?
questions.explain: Editing the master slide changes the design of every slide at once. Slide transition is tempting because it can be applied to all slides, but it controls movement between slides, not the design itself.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an ADVANCED feature of graphic software?
questions.explain: Layers let separate elements be edited independently, which is an advanced feature. Cropping is tempting because it changes the image noticeably, but cropping and resizing are basic features.

questions.stem: A school wants to send 300 personalised letters to parents using a shared list of names and addresses. Which combination of software is MOST appropriate?
options: Word processing (mail merge) combined with a spreadsheet or database
questions.explain: Mail merge in a word processor joins the standard letter with the address list held in a spreadsheet or database. "Spreadsheet only" is tempting because the list is in a spreadsheet, but a spreadsheet alone cannot produce formatted personalised letters.

questions.stem: Which of the following file extensions is associated with presentation software?
questions.explain: .pptx is the Microsoft PowerPoint format. .accdb is tempting because it is less familiar, but it is the Microsoft Access database format.

questions.stem: Leon changes the name of his file from Report.docx to Report.pdf by typing over the extension. Which of the following is MOST likely to happen?
options: The file is automatically uploaded to the cloud.
The file becomes a web-based document.
The file is converted into a proper PDF.
The file may become unreadable or open in the wrong application.
questions.explain: Changing an extension by hand does not convert the file's actual format, so it may not open correctly. Option C is tempting, but only Save As or Export converts the contents.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of web-based application software rather than computer-based application software?
options: It works without any internet access.
Several users can edit the same file at the same time.
It is tied to the device on which it is installed.
It must be installed on the hard drive.
questions.explain: Real-time collaboration is typical of web-based software such as Google Docs. "Works without internet" is tempting because it sounds like an advantage, but that describes computer-based software.

questions.stem: A teacher wants every mark below 50 in her grade sheet to turn red automatically. Which spreadsheet feature should she use?
questions.explain: Conditional formatting changes the appearance of cells that meet a condition. Data validation is tempting because it also uses conditions, but it controls what may be entered, not how cells look.

questions.stem: Which spreadsheet feature restricts what can be entered into a cell in order to reduce input errors?
questions.explain: Data validation restricts entries, e.g. only whole numbers from 0 to 100. Conditional formatting is the tempting distractor, but it only changes appearance after data is entered.

questions.stem: In a database table of students, which field is MOST suitable as the primary key?
questions.explain: A primary key must uniquely identify each record, and a student ID does. A parent's phone number is tempting because it is a number, but siblings may share it and it can change.

questions.stem: A field in one table that refers to the primary key of another table is called a
questions.explain: A foreign key creates the link between related tables. "Query" is tempting because queries often use related tables, but a query retrieves data; it is not a field.

questions.stem: The librarian needs a list of books that are overdue AND were borrowed by Form 4 students. Which database feature is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: A query retrieves a precise subset of data using combined conditions. A form is tempting because it displays records, but it is for entering or viewing data one record at a time, not for selecting by conditions.

questions.stem: Which presentation feature allows a presenter to read private reminders while delivering a speech?
questions.explain: Speaker notes are visible to the presenter but not to the audience. Master slide is tempting because it is another advanced feature, but it controls design, not the presenter's notes.

questions.stem: A company logo must be printed on a business card and on a large billboard without losing quality. It should be created as a
questions.explain: Vector images are built from mathematical paths and scale to any size without loss of quality. A raster image is tempting because photos are common, but raster images blur when enlarged significantly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST reason for a presenter to adjust an inserted graphic to suit the content and context of a slide?
options: To ensure the graphic supports the message and suits the audience and design
To make the file size larger
To avoid using any text on the slide
Because unedited graphics cannot be displayed in slide show mode
questions.explain: Adjusting a graphic keeps it relevant to the content and appropriate to the context, which makes the presentation clearer and more professional. Option D is tempting because it sounds technical, but unedited graphics display perfectly well; they just may not suit the slide.

questions.stem: A parent-teacher association needs to track membership fees paid by 150 families and calculate the total collected each term. Which software is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: The task is mainly calculation, and a spreadsheet's formulas total the fees and recalculate as payments are added. Word processing is tempting because the list includes names, but a word processor table cannot calculate and update totals.

questions.stem: In the Dox to Go (D2G) case study, which software was used to condense key figures into a five-slide summary for the manager's Monday briefing?
questions.explain: A slide summary for a live briefing is produced in presentation software. Word processing is tempting because it produced the full written report, but the slides came from presentation software at the final stage.

questions.stem: Which of the following tasks is BEST suited to graphic software?
options: Storing borrower records for a library
Editing a photograph before inserting it into a newsletter
questions.explain: Editing photographs is a core use of graphic software, which then enhances the newsletter. Drafting minutes is tempting because a newsletter is also a text document, but minutes need only word processing.

questions.stem: Which alignment stretches text so that it meets both the left and right margins?
questions.explain: Justified alignment spaces out each line so it touches both margins, as in newsletters. Left alignment is tempting because it is the standard for body text, but it leaves the right edge ragged.

questions.stem: A faint image or text placed behind a document's main content to indicate its status is called a
questions.explain: A watermark such as DRAFT or CONFIDENTIAL shows status without hiding the text. A header is tempting because it also repeats on every page, but it sits in the top margin, not behind the content.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST appropriate font choice for the body of a printed business letter?
options: A decorative script font in 16 pt
Three different fonts to add interest
Times New Roman 12 pt in black
questions.explain: A legible, professional font at 10 to 12 point in black or dark grey is standard. Arial is a good font, which makes the last option tempting, but 8 pt in light yellow is too small and too faint to read.

questions.stem: Footnotes differ from endnotes because footnotes
options: appear at the bottom of the page on which they are referenced
appear at the end of the document
questions.explain: Footnotes sit at the foot of the relevant page; endnotes are collected at the end of the document or chapter. "Repeat on every page" describes headers and footers, a common confusion.

questions.stem: A list of steps for logging in to the school portal should be formatted as a
questions.explain: Numbering shows sequence, so it suits step-by-step instructions. A bulleted list is tempting because it is also a list, but bullets are for items with no particular order.

questions.stem: Which editing technique automatically substitutes one word or phrase with another throughout a document?
questions.explain: Find and Replace locates and substitutes text throughout the document. Search is tempting because it also locates the word, but it does not change anything.
