questions.stem: In Overtype (type over) mode, new characters
options: are inserted, pushing existing text forward
replace existing text at the cursor position
questions.explain: Overtype writes over the characters at the cursor. Pushing text forward is what insert mode does, which is why the first option is the most tempting distractor.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the difference between cut and copy?
options: Copy deletes the original; cut duplicates it.
Cut uses the clipboard; copy does not.
Cut removes the selection and places it on the clipboard; copy leaves the original in place.
questions.explain: Both cut and copy place the selection on the clipboard; only cut removes the original. Option C is tempting, but copy also uses the clipboard. It is drag and drop (move) that bypasses the clipboard.

questions.stem: A typist runs the spelling check and it finds no errors, yet the letter contains "Please call form Monday". This shows that
options: the thesaurus should have been used
Find and Replace was used incorrectly
the spelling check is switched off
spelling checks cannot detect correctly spelt words used wrongly, so manual proofreading is essential
questions.explain: "Form" is a real word, so spelling check accepts it. Only careful proofreading catches such errors. The thesaurus is tempting, but it suggests synonyms; it does not detect errors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a simple tabulation skill, rather than an advanced one?
options: Applying borders and aligning a table on the page
Inserting a chart from table data
questions.explain: Borders and table alignment are listed under simple tabulations. Conditional formatting is tempting because it also changes appearance, but it is an advanced formatting feature.

questions.stem: A column heading whose text is slanted at an angle of about 45° so that it fits above a narrow column is called
questions.explain: Oblique means slanted. A vertical heading is tempting because it also rotates the text to save horizontal space, but a vertical heading is turned fully on its side (90°), not slanted.

questions.stem: Which predefined function would return the highest score in a range of student marks?
questions.explain: MAX returns the largest value. MIN is the tempting wrong answer because it also returns a single value from the range, but it returns the smallest.

questions.stem: Cells B2 to B5 contain 40, 25, 60 and 35. What value will =AVERAGE(B2:B5) return?
questions.explain: The total is 160 and there are 4 values, so the average is 160 / 4 = 40. 160 is tempting because it is the SUM, but the average divides the total by the count.

questions.stem: Which formula correctly multiplies the quantity in B3 by the price in C3?
questions.explain: A formula begins with = and uses * for multiplication. =SUM(B3:C3) is tempting because it is a valid formula, but it adds the two cells instead of multiplying them.

questions.stem: According to your syllabus, a simple database at this level should be populated using no more than
questions.explain: The syllabus states no more than five fields. Two is tempting because simple queries use one or two fields, but that limit applies to the query, not the table.

questions.stem: In a database table, all the information about ONE student is called a
questions.explain: A record is one row: everything about one person or item. A field is tempting, but a field is one category (column) of data for every record.

questions.stem: Which data type is MOST suitable for a field storing telephone numbers such as +1 246 555 0148?
questions.explain: Phone numbers contain symbols and spaces and are never calculated, so Text is correct. Number is tempting because the entry is mostly digits, but a Number field would reject the + and the spaces.

questions.stem: The school office wants a printed, titled list of only the students in Form 4B. Which sequence is correct?
options: Run a query on the Form Class field with the criterion 4B, then generate a report from the query
Create a report, then sort the table
Delete all other records, then print the table
questions.explain: A query selects the matching records and a report presents them. Deleting records is tempting because it also leaves only 4B, but it destroys data the school still needs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a criterion for selecting an image to include in a document?
questions.explain: Relevance, quality, appropriateness and licensing are the criteria. File size is tempting because large files can slow a document, but it is not one of the selection criteria.

questions.stem: Combining several separate graphic elements into a single object that can be moved or resized as one unit is called
questions.explain: Grouping combines objects into one unit. Ungrouping is the tempting distractor because it involves the same objects, but it separates them again.

questions.stem: To make a logo smaller without distorting it, the user should
options: drag a corner handle or lock the aspect ratio
questions.explain: Proportional resizing keeps the height and width in the same ratio. Dragging a side handle is tempting because it does change the size, but it stretches or squashes the image.

questions.stem: Which presentation element controls how long each slide is displayed before advancing to the next?
questions.explain: Timing sets how long a slide stays on screen. Transition is tempting because it happens as the slide advances, but it controls how the change looks, not when it happens.

questions.stem: An effect that makes one bullet point fly in when the presenter clicks is BEST described as
questions.explain: Animations act on objects within a slide. A transition is tempting, but transitions act between slides.

questions.stem: Mail merge is an example of
options: integration of information from different software
questions.explain: Mail merge combines a word-processed main document with data from a spreadsheet or database. Simple tabulation is tempting because the data source is often a table, but the merge itself is integration.

questions.stem: Inserting a chart built in a spreadsheet directly into a word-processed report, rather than retyping the figures, is an example of using
questions.explain: The figures come from another application, so they are an external data source; this avoids retyping errors. A footnote is tempting because it adds information to a report, but it does not import data.

questions.stem: Which paper orientation is wider than it is tall?
questions.explain: Landscape is wider than it is tall and suits wide tables, charts and certificates. Legal is tempting because it sounds like a layout, but Legal and Letter are paper SIZES, not orientations.

questions.stem: Which international paper size is the standard for most letters and business documents?
questions.explain: A4 (21 cm x 29.7 cm) is the international standard for business documents. A3 is tempting because it is also common, but at twice the size of A4 it is used for posters and large charts.

questions.stem: A DL envelope is specifically designed to hold a sheet of A4 paper folded
questions.explain: DL (11 cm x 22 cm) takes A4 folded twice, into thirds. "In half" is tempting, but A4 folded once fits a C5 envelope.

questions.stem: Which paper size measures 21.6 cm x 35.6 cm (8.5" x 14") and is used for contracts and legal agreements?
questions.explain: Legal paper is the same width as Letter but longer (14"), giving room for long contracts. Letter is tempting because it shares the 8.5" width, but it is only 11" long.

questions.stem: Coral Reef Hardware wants to collect the same details (name, item, quantity, delivery date) from every customer who places a special order. The MOST appropriate stationery is
questions.explain: A form has fixed fields, so every customer supplies the same information in the same format. Letterhead is tempting because it is used with customers, but it is for correspondence, not for collecting standard information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is LEAST likely to appear in a business letterhead?
options: The telephone number and e-mail address
questions.explain: The letterhead identifies the SENDER; the recipient's name belongs in the inside address. A logo is tempting because it is optional, but it is a normal part of many letterheads.

questions.stem: In a blocked letter, where does every line, including the date and closing, begin?
questions.explain: In blocked style everything begins at the left margin. "Indented one tab stop" is tempting, but indented first lines are the mark of the indented style.

questions.stem: A letter has paragraphs beginning at the left margin, but its date and complimentary close are positioned toward the right. This letter is in
questions.explain: Blocked paragraphs plus a right-positioned date and close is semi-blocked. Indented is tempting because the date is on the right, but an indented letter also indents the first line of each paragraph.

questions.stem: Which of the following lines is correctly set out in OPEN punctuation?
questions.explain: Open punctuation uses no punctuation outside the body, so "Mr K Gumbs" with no full stops is correct. "Dear Mr. Gumbs," is tempting because it is a common style, but the full stop and comma make it closed punctuation.

questions.stem: Which part of a business letter comes IMMEDIATELY after the salutation?
questions.explain: The order is salutation, then subject heading, then body. The inside address is tempting because it is near the salutation, but it comes BEFORE it.

questions.stem: A letter begins "Dear Sir or Madam". The correct complimentary close is
questions.explain: An unnamed salutation is paired with Yours faithfully. Yours sincerely is tempting because it is also formal, but it is used when the reader is named.

questions.stem: The heading at the top of the second page of a two-page letter should include the
options: page number, date and recipient's name
questions.explain: A continuation heading shows the page number, date and recipient's name, on plain paper. The full letterhead is tempting for consistency, but letterhead is used for page 1 only.

questions.stem: A letter sent in identical or near-identical form to many recipients is called a
questions.explain: A circular letter goes to many recipients, often with a table, inset or enumeration. A memorandum is tempting because it may also go to many people, but a memo is for internal communication only.

questions.stem: In a circular letter, an important closing date is typed as a block indented from both margins so that it stands out. This is called
questions.explain: An inset is text indented from the margin(s) to make it stand out. Enumeration is tempting because it also organises information, but enumeration means numbering or lettering points.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MAIN advantage of mail merge over manual preparation of envelopes?
options: It removes the need to proofread.
It is the best method for a single envelope.
Many personalised envelopes or labels can be produced quickly and consistently.
questions.explain: Mail merge combines a template with a data source to produce many personalised items at once. Option A is tempting, but errors in the data source are copied to every label, so proofreading is still essential.

questions.stem: Where is a special notation such as CONFIDENTIAL typed on an envelope?
options: In the lower-left corner or above the recipient's address
questions.explain: Notations go in the lower-left corner or just above the address, in capitals, where handlers see them at once. The top-right corner is tempting because it is prominent, but it is kept clear for the stamp.

questions.stem: Which special notation would MOST likely be used on an envelope containing a company's sensitive financial data?
questions.explain: CONFIDENTIAL means the contents are sensitive and should be opened only by the named addressee. PERSONAL is tempting because it also restricts opening, but it signals that the letter concerns the recipient as an individual, not sensitive business data.

questions.stem: Skeleton notes are BEST described as
options: brief, incomplete notes that must be expanded into full correspondence
questions.explain: Skeleton notes are key points or fragments from which you compose complete correspondence. "An audio recording only" is tempting because you also compose from voice messages, but skeleton notes are written fragments, and recordings are a different source.

questions.stem: When composing a letter from a manager's voice message, which step is MOST important to avoid errors such as "fifteen" being typed as "fifty"?
options: Typing while listening for the first time
Proofreading the finished document against the recording
questions.explain: Recordings are easily misheard, so you must check names and figures against the source before printing. Typing during the first listen is tempting to save time, but you should listen to the whole message first to understand it.

questions.stem: Which heading elements are standard on EVERY memorandum, regardless of style?
questions.explain: Every memo has the TO, FROM, DATE and SUBJECT heading block. Inside address and salutation are tempting because they appear in letters, but memos do not use them.

questions.stem: A memo in which the first line of each paragraph begins away from the left margin is a(n)
questions.explain: In an indented memo the first line of each paragraph is indented. Short and long describe LENGTH, not alignment, so they cannot be the answer even if the memo happens to be short.

questions.stem: Which meeting document is prepared specifically for the chairperson and includes notes beside each item and a blank column for notes?
questions.explain: The chairman's agenda expands each item with background notes and leaves a NOTES column for the chair. Minutes are tempting because they also contain notes, but minutes are the official record written after the meeting.

questions.stem: Which meeting document is prepared AFTER a meeting, recording what was discussed and decided?
questions.explain: Minutes are the official record, prepared after the meeting. The chairman's agenda is tempting because the chair writes on it during the meeting, but those are private notes, not the official record.

questions.stem: Which of the following lines is correctly written for the minutes of a meeting?
options: I said the stall will make lots of money.
It was agreed that the Club would hold a car wash on 14 November.
Dear Members, the car wash is on 14 November.
Ms Lake says she will buy the soap.
questions.explain: Minutes are in the third person, past tense, recording decisions: "It was agreed that...". Option D is tempting because it names a person and a task, but it uses present and future tense; it should read "Ms Lake agreed to buy the soap."

questions.stem: When inserting a chart into a business document, text wrapping should generally be set so that
options: the surrounding text flows neatly around or above and below the graphic
the chart is placed on a separate, unrelated page
questions.explain: Wrapping should let the text flow neatly around the graphic without overlapping it, and the graphic should sit close to its related text. Option B is tempting because it keeps the page clean, but readers must be able to connect the chart to the text immediately.

questions.stem: Columnar information separated visually using lines between rows and columns is described as
questions.explain: Ruled work uses lines (rules) between rows and/or columns. Unruled work is tempting because it is also columnar, but it is aligned with tab stops and spacing only, with no visible lines.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a single-page promotional document designed to catch attention quickly?
questions.explain: A flyer combines a bold headline, concise text and graphics on one page to promote something. A notice might seem close, but a notice informs rather than promotes; the other options are financial and legal documents.

questions.stem: A notice is to be centred so that the space above the text equals the space below it. This is BEST described as
questions.explain: Vertical centring balances the block of text from top to bottom on the page. Horizontal centring is tempting, but it balances each line from left to right, not top to bottom.

questions.stem: A notice contains 24 lines including blank lines and is to be centred vertically on A4 paper holding 70 lines. How many blank lines should be left at the top?
questions.explain: 70 minus 24 = 46; 46 divided by 2 = 23. Option C (46) is tempting because it is the first step of the sum, but leaving all 46 blank lines at the top would push the notice to the bottom of the page.

questions.stem: Leader dots are MOST likely to be used in
options: the signature block of a will
a programme, linking each item to the person responsible
questions.explain: Leader dots lead the eye across a gap from an item to its matching entry, as in programmes and menus. A signature block uses lines for signing, not leader dots, so option B is a distractor.

questions.stem: Which diagram shows the hierarchy and reporting relationships within an organisation?
questions.explain: An organisation chart shows who reports to whom, from the top position down. A flow chart is tempting because it is also a diagram, but it shows the steps of a process, not people and positions.

questions.stem: In a flow chart, a diamond-shaped symbol represents
options: the start or end of the process
questions.explain: The diamond is the decision symbol, with two exits labelled YES and NO. The oval is tempting for students who remember "special shapes", but the oval marks start and end only.

questions.stem: A graph that automatically updates whenever its source data changes is described as
questions.explain: A linked graph stays connected to its source spreadsheet and updates when the data changes. Embedded is the tempting opposite: an embedded graph is a fixed snapshot that does not update.

questions.stem: A school must file its 2025 Annual Report showing exam results exactly as they were presented to the Board. Which type of graph is MOST appropriate?
options: A linked graph, so it always shows the newest results
An embedded graph, so it preserves the data as it stood at that time
No graph, because reports cannot contain charts
questions.explain: An embedded graph preserves a fixed record of the data. A linked graph is tempting because it sounds more up to date, but it would change as new data is entered and would no longer match the filed report.

questions.stem: On a 4-page leaflet made from one A4 sheet folded once, which pages are printed on the same side as the front cover (page 1)?
questions.explain: The outside of the sheet carries page 4 (back cover) beside page 1 (front cover); pages 2 and 3 are printed on the inside. Pages 2 and 3 are tempting because they follow page 1 in reading order, but they are on the reverse side.

questions.stem: Each continuation page of a multi-page document should carry
options: the recipient's name, the page number and the date
questions.explain: A continuation heading of name, page number and date lets separated pages be identified and put back together. The full letterhead is tempting, but it appears on the first page only; continuation pages use plain paper.

questions.stem: In a press release, the opening paragraph should typically answer
options: who, what, when, where and why
only the price of the product
questions.explain: The lead gives the essential facts (the five Ws) so a journalist can use the story at once. Background history is tempting because it may appear in a press release, but it belongs briefly near the end, not in the lead.

questions.stem: Which document formally transfers ownership of property from one party to another?
questions.explain: A conveyance document transfers ownership from the vendor to the purchaser. A lease is the tempting distractor, but a lease only allows the lessee to use the property for a period; ownership stays with the lessor.

questions.stem: An insurance company adds flood cover to an existing home insurance policy. The document used to do this is a(n)
questions.explain: An endorsement adds, amends or confirms terms on an existing document such as an insurance policy. A conveyance document is tempting because it also deals with property, but it transfers ownership rather than changing a policy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is BEST practice when keying a sum of money in a legal agreement?
options: Words and figures, e.g. two thousand five hundred United States dollars (US$2,500.00)
questions.explain: Writing the sum in words and figures means it cannot be misread or altered. Figures only (option C) is tempting because it is quicker, but a figure is easy to change or mistype, which could alter the obligation.

questions.stem: A signature block reserved at the end of a legal document is intended for
options: the parties (and, where required, a witness) to sign and date
questions.explain: The signature block is where the parties, and a witness where required, sign and date the document to make it binding. A logo is tempting for students thinking of letterheads, but logos belong at the top, not in the signature block.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a technical document used for costing and procurement on a construction project?
questions.explain: A bill of quantity itemises materials, parts and labour with quantities, rates and amounts for costing and ordering. A balance sheet is tempting because it contains figures, but it shows a business's financial position, not project materials.

questions.stem: Which technical document defines exactly what work will and will NOT be carried out on a project?
questions.explain: A scope of works sets the boundaries of a project, including exclusions. A specification is tempting because it is also technical, but it describes the materials, methods and standards rather than what is in and out of the project.

questions.stem: Which literary document is formatted with detailed sound cues because its audience relies entirely on dialogue and sound?
questions.explain: A radio audience can only hear, so radio scripts use detailed SFX and MUSIC cues. A television play is tempting because it also uses sound, but it relies on scene headings and camera directions for what the viewer sees.

questions.stem: The line "INT. CLASSROOM – DAY" would MOST likely appear in a script for
questions.explain: Scene headings showing interior or exterior, location and time are a television (screen) convention. Theatre is tempting because it has scenes too, but theatre uses ACT and SCENE headings with stage directions, not INT./EXT. headings.

questions.stem: Which financial statement shows a business's assets, liabilities and owner's equity at a specific point in time?
questions.explain: The balance sheet is a snapshot of financial position "as at" a date. The profit and loss statement is tempting because it is also a final account, but it covers income and expenses over a period.

questions.stem: A church youth group wants to show the money it received and spent during the year. Which statement should its treasurer prepare?
questions.explain: Non-profit organisations normally prepare an income and expenditure statement, showing a surplus or deficit. A profit and loss statement is tempting because it is similar, but it is used by businesses that aim to make a profit.

questions.stem: A document confirming that payment has been made for goods or services is called a(n)
questions.explain: A receipt is proof of payment. The invoice is the most tempting distractor, but an invoice is a request for payment issued before the money is paid.

questions.stem: Which of the following is BEST practice when formatting figures in a financial statement?
options: Right-align or decimal-align figures with consistent decimal places and clearly marked totals
Use a different currency symbol on each line
Centre all figures in their columns
Place totals in the same style as the line items
questions.explain: Right or decimal alignment keeps the decimal points in line for comparison, and totals are distinguished with rules or bold. Centring is tempting because it looks tidy, but centred figures of different lengths do not line up and are hard to add.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes creating a template WITHOUT a wizard?
options: Building the layout and formatting manually from a blank document and saving it as a template file type
Printing a document without saving it
Using a step-by-step prompt that generates a document automatically
Copying a completed document and deleting its content
questions.explain: The manual method means building everything yourself and saving it as a template type such as .dotx. Copying a completed document is tempting, but the result is an ordinary document that is easily overwritten, not a template.

questions.stem: Which type of electronic communication scans a physical document and sends it directly to a specified e-mail address?
questions.explain: Scan to mail sends the digital copy straight to an e-mail address. Scan to file is the tempting distractor, but it saves the copy to a folder or storage location instead of e-mailing it.

questions.stem: Which e-mail feature allows a sender to copy in additional recipients WITHOUT revealing their addresses to one another?
questions.explain: Blind Carbon Copy hides the addresses of those recipients. Cc is tempting because it also sends a copy, but everyone in To and Cc can see who else received the message.

questions.stem: A short, specific summary of an e-mail's content is entered in the
questions.explain: The subject line summarises the content so the reader understands the purpose at a glance and can search for it later. The signature block is tempting because it is also a standard part of an e-mail, but it identifies the sender, not the content.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an ADVANTAGE of electronic communication?
options: Sending information to multiple recipients simultaneously
Challenges ensuring the message is received
High cost compared with postal mail
questions.explain: One message can reach many people at once without retyping or reprinting. "High cost" is tempting only if misread; electronic communication is generally far cheaper than postal mail.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a DISADVANTAGE of electronic communication?
options: Challenges ensuring the message is received
questions.explain: Messages can be missed, filtered into spam or overlooked, leaving the sender unsure whether they were seen. Speed of delivery is tempting because it can indirectly cause errors, but on its own it is listed as an advantage.

questions.stem: Which new or emerging communication technology relies PRIMARILY on video content?
questions.explain: Vlogging is video-based, relying on visual and spoken communication. Blogging is the tempting distractor because both publish content regularly, but blogging is text-based.

questions.stem: Sorting e-mail by grouping all messages from a specific client together is an example of sorting by
questions.explain: Grouping by who sent the messages is sorting by sender. Subject is tempting, but it groups messages by topic or thread, which could mix many clients together.

questions.stem: Moving older, completed correspondence out of the main inbox into long-term storage is called
questions.explain: Archiving keeps the inbox manageable while preserving the messages for future reference or audits. Deleting is tempting because it also clears the inbox, but deleted messages are not preserved.

questions.stem: A highly urgent, time-sensitive message would generally be BEST suited to
options: a medium chosen for real-time or near-instant delivery
a medium with no regard for confidentiality
a medium chosen for low cost only
questions.explain: Urgency calls for an instant medium such as a phone call or instant message. Choosing for low cost alone is tempting because cost is a real factor, but it ignores the factor that matters most here.

questions.stem: Writing an e-mail entirely in capital letters is generally understood in netiquette as
options: a way to show the message is urgent and polite
questions.explain: All capitals are widely read as shouting. Some writers think capitals show urgency, which makes the last option tempting, but they come across as rude, not polite.

questions.stem: Coordinating a project team spread across three different countries would MOST directly involve which factor in selecting communication media?
questions.explain: Team members in different countries may be in different time zones, which affects whether a real-time call is practical. Cost is tempting because international communication can be expensive, but location and time zone are the most direct factor.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes "reflective" communication technologies?
options: Technologies that allow the audience to respond, comment or interact directly
Technologies that only broadcast information one way
Technologies that cannot be used for business
questions.explain: Reflective technologies support two-way, participatory exchange. The one-way option is tempting because it describes older communication, but that is broadcast-style, the opposite of reflective.

questions.stem: A receptionist must store 50 scanned delivery notes in the Accounts folder on the shared drive. Which multifunctional device feature should she use?
questions.explain: Scan to file saves the digital copies directly to a specified folder. Scan to mail is tempting, but it sends the copies to an inbox rather than storing them in the folder.

questions.stem: Platforms built around user-generated content, such as Internet forums, weblogs and podcasts, are classified as
questions.explain: The syllabus lists forums, weblogs and podcasts as examples of social media. Social networking might come to mind, but it focuses on building connections, and it is not one of the options here.

questions.stem: A manager e-mails the finance officer, who must approve a budget, and wants the principal to be kept informed without being expected to act. The principal's address should go in the
questions.explain: Cc is for recipients who should be kept informed but are not expected to act. The To field is tempting, but it is for the primary recipient who must act, which here is the finance officer.

questions.stem: An administrator e-mails a client what she thinks is the signed contract, but it turns out to be an outdated draft. This is an example of
options: a challenge ensuring the message is received
questions.explain: Sending an incorrect attachment is an error in dispatch. A challenge ensuring receipt is tempting because both are disadvantages, but here the message arrived; the problem is that the wrong file was sent.

questions.stem: Which of the following practices would BEST reduce the challenge of ensuring an important e-mail is received?
options: Sending it to as many people as possible
Writing the message in capital letters
Asking the recipient to confirm receipt and following up if there is no reply
questions.explain: Confirming receipt and following up deals directly with the uncertainty of whether the message was seen. Sending it to many people is tempting, but it creates new privacy and dispatch risks without confirming that the intended person saw it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the KEY feature of smartphones as an emerging communication technology?
options: They are text-based and organised by date or category.
They combine multiple communication channels in one portable, always-connected device.
They transmit documents over a telephone line to a fax machine.
questions.explain: Smartphones bring calling, messaging, e-mail, browsing and apps into one portable device. The first option is tempting because people read blogs on phones, but text-based posts organised by date describe blogging.

questions.stem: A sales manager wants to read every e-mail about the "Arima showroom project" from the first quotation to the final invoice. Which sorting method is MOST useful?
questions.explain: Sorting by subject keeps a whole conversation thread or project together from start to finish. Sorting by sender is tempting, but several people (suppliers, builders, the accountant) wrote about the project, so their messages would be split up.

questions.stem: A well-maintained contact list MAINLY reduces the risk of
options: messages being written in capital letters
messages being sent to an outdated address or the wrong person
questions.explain: Keeping contacts current and grouped means messages go to the right, up-to-date address. Spam filtering is tempting because it also stops messages reaching people, but it is controlled by the recipient's e-mail system, not the sender's contact list.

questions.stem: A supervisor must discuss a sensitive disciplinary matter with an employee. Which medium is MOST appropriate?
options: A message in the staff group chat
questions.explain: A sensitive matter calls for a confidential, oral medium such as a face-to-face meeting or phone call. A bulk e-mail is tempting because e-mail is the usual office medium, but it is impersonal and can easily be forwarded.

questions.stem: Instructions for assembling a new piece of equipment would be MOST effectively communicated using which genre?
options: A fax of a handwritten note
Written, as a long e-mail paragraph
Visual, such as a video or diagram
Oral, such as a phone call
questions.explain: Step-by-step physical instructions are best shown, so the visual genre is most effective. A written e-mail is tempting because it provides a record, but readers can misunderstand physical steps described only in words.

questions.stem: An e-mail claiming to be from a bank asks you to click a link and enter your password "within one hour or your account will be closed". According to safe online practice, you should
options: reply with your password so the bank can check it
verify the sender by contacting the bank through its official number and not click the link
forward it to all your colleagues as a warning with the link active
click the link quickly to avoid losing the account
questions.explain: Netiquette and safety require you to verify unfamiliar senders and be cautious with suspicious links, which may be fraud or malware. Forwarding it as a warning is tempting because it seems helpful, but spreading an active suspicious link puts colleagues at risk.

questions.stem: Netiquette is BEST defined as
options: the accepted standards of polite, professional and ethical behaviour when communicating electronically
the speed at which a network sends data
questions.explain: Netiquette combines "net" and "etiquette": accepted standards of polite, professional and ethical online behaviour. The archiving option is tempting because both relate to e-mail, but archiving is a file organisation method.

questions.stem: Which type of filing system stores documents as physical paper in folders and cabinets?
questions.explain: A manual filing system stores documents in physical form, such as paper in folders, binders or cabinets. "Electronic" is tempting only because it is the other filing system; it stores documents digitally. Machine-readable and turnaround are types of document, not filing systems.

questions.stem: A completed order form, filled in by hand before being entered into a computer system, is an example of a
questions.explain: A source document is the original document on which data is FIRST recorded before it is entered into the system. A turnaround document is tempting, but it must first be produced by the system and sent out, which an order form filled in by hand is not.

questions.stem: A utility bill stub that is returned by the customer along with payment for further processing is an example of a
questions.explain: The stub was produced by the system, sent out, and returned as input, which is the definition of a turnaround document. It may also carry a barcode, which makes "machine-readable" tempting, but the question stresses that it is returned for further processing.

questions.stem: In an electronic filing system, which level of the hierarchy sits directly ABOVE individual files?
questions.explain: Files are stored inside folders or sub-folders, so the folder sits directly above them. The drive is tempting because it is the top of the hierarchy, but it sits above the folders, not directly above the files.

questions.stem: Which file integrity measure allows a user to VIEW a file's content but prevents them from saving any changes to it?
questions.explain: Read-only access lets a user view a file but not make or save changes. Encryption is tempting because it also protects content, but it makes the content unreadable to people without the key rather than allowing viewing without editing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a CYBER security measure?
questions.explain: A firewall is a software or hardware barrier that controls network traffic, so it is a cyber measure. The fireproof cabinet is tempting because of the word "fire", but it is physical storage.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a PHYSICAL security measure?
questions.explain: Fireproof and waterproof storage protects paper records and hardware from physical damage. Passwords, firewalls and encryption are digital (cyber) measures; encryption is tempting because it "locks" data, but only digitally.

questions.stem: Moving older, less frequently used files out of active storage into long-term, organised storage is called
questions.explain: This is the definition of archiving. Versioning is tempting because it also involves older copies, but versioning keeps successive versions of one changing document; it does not move files into long-term storage.

questions.stem: Which metadata field records when a file's content was most recently changed?
questions.explain: Date modified records the most recent change to the content. Date accessed is the most tempting distractor, but it records when the file was last opened, even if nothing was changed.

questions.stem: Preserving successive saved copies of a document as it changes over time is called
questions.explain: Versioning keeps Version 1, Version 2 and so on, so earlier states can be reviewed or restored. Metadata is tempting because it also supports traceability, but it is data about the file (dates, owner), not the saved copies themselves.

questions.stem: Which document type is specifically formatted so its data can be read directly by a scanning device?
questions.explain: A machine-readable document (barcode, QR code, OMR sheet) is read directly by a machine without manual re-entry. A turnaround document is tempting because many carry barcodes, but its defining feature is that it is returned as input.

questions.stem: A business backs up its files only to a second hard drive kept in the same office. This practice is a weakness in
options: cyber security only, with no physical security risk.
both cyber and physical security, since a single disaster could destroy both copies.
questions.explain: A fire, flood or hurricane could destroy both drives, and an attack on the office system could reach both, so it is a weakness in both kinds of security. "Cyber security only" is tempting, but it ignores the obvious physical risk of keeping both copies in one room.

questions.stem: Which of the following is BEST described as an advantage of an electronic filing system over a manual one?
options: Staff need no training to use it.
It does not depend on electricity.
Files can be searched quickly by name, date or keyword.
It cannot be damaged in any way.
questions.explain: Rapid search and retrieval is a key advantage of electronic filing. Option B is tempting, but independence from electricity is an advantage of MANUAL filing. Electronic files can be damaged (hardware failure, cyberattack) and staff do need training.

questions.stem: A sales manager's laptop holding client accounts is stolen from her car. Which measure would BEST prevent the thief from reading the files?
questions.explain: Encryption converts content into a coded form that cannot be read without the key, even if the device is stolen. Read-only access is tempting, but it only stops changes; a thief could still read a read-only file.

questions.stem: Which of the following file names follows good electronic filing practice?
questions.explain: This name is clear and descriptive and uses the YYYY-MM-DD date format. "new final FINAL" is tempting because it suggests the latest copy, but it does not describe the content and causes confusion when more changes are made.

questions.stem: Why do organisations write dates in file names in the format YYYY-MM-DD?
options: Files sort correctly in date order.
It is required by the operating system.
questions.explain: Because computers sort names character by character, YYYY-MM-DD puts files into date order automatically. Option B is tempting, but the operating system accepts many date formats; the format is a naming convention, not a requirement.

questions.stem: A message appears: "A file named 'Budget.xlsx' already exists. Do you want to replace it?" This is an example of
questions.explain: The warning stops an existing file being unintentionally replaced by a new file with the same name, which is overwrite protection. Restricted access is tempting because it also protects files, but it controls WHO can open or edit, not accidental replacement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a risk of retaining files for LONGER than necessary?
options: Unnecessary storage costs and greater exposure if the data is breached
Being unable to produce records for an audit
questions.explain: Keeping files too long costs storage and increases the amount of data that could be stolen in a breach. Option C is tempting, but being unable to produce records is a risk of disposing of files too SOON.

questions.stem: Which is the MOST appropriate way to dispose of paper customer records that contain credit-card details once their retention period has ended?
options: Move them to a different filing cabinet
Place them in the recycling bin intact
questions.explain: Secure disposal, such as shredding, ensures sensitive information is not left accessible. Archiving is tempting, but the retention period has ended, and archiving keeps the records rather than disposing of them.

questions.stem: Metadata is BEST described as
options: the visible text of a document.
the font and layout of a document.
data about a document, such as its owner and date modified.
a backup copy of a document.
questions.explain: Metadata is data stored about a document rather than in its visible content. Option A is tempting because metadata is "data", but the visible text is the content itself, not data about it.

questions.stem: A clerk drags a file from the desktop into the 'Invoices' folder on the same drive. Afterwards the file is no longer on the desktop. Which operation has she carried out?
questions.explain: Moving takes the file out of one location and places it in another, leaving one copy. Copy is tempting, but a copy would leave the original on the desktop as well.

questions.stem: A disaster recovery mechanism is BEST described as
options: a list of how long each document must be kept.
a setting that prevents files from being edited.
a documented plan and system for restoring data and operations quickly after a disaster.
a program that blocks network traffic.
questions.explain: Disaster recovery mechanisms are plans and systems to restore data and operations after a cyberattack, system failure or physical disaster. Option D is tempting because firewalls are also security measures, but blocking traffic is the job of a firewall.

questions.stem: A school wants only the principal and the bursar to be able to open the staff salary spreadsheet. Which file integrity measure is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Restricted access uses user accounts and permissions to limit who may open, edit or delete a file. Read-only access is tempting, but it would still allow other staff to VIEW the salaries.

questions.stem: Intellectual property is BEST described as
options: the creations of the mind, such as inventions and artistic works
the hardware used to store documents
a category of computer file extension
any physical object owned by a business
questions.explain: Intellectual property refers to the creations of the mind, such as inventions, literary and artistic works, designs, symbols, names and images. Option D is tempting because the word "property" suggests physical objects, but intellectual property is intangible: its value lies in the original idea, not the object that carries it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a LITERARY work?
options: The shape of a designer chair
questions.explain: Song lyrics are written words, so they are listed with literary works such as novels, poems and articles. The designer chair (B) is tempting because it is creative, but the distinctive appearance of a product is a design, not a literary work.

questions.stem: A creator's right to be paid when others use their work is known as a(n)
questions.explain: Economic rights cover payment for use, such as royalties and licensing fees. Moral rights (B) are the most tempting distractor, but they protect the integrity and reputation of the work, not payment.

questions.stem: A newspaper misquotes a novelist so that she appears to support a view she opposes. Which right has MOST directly been violated?
questions.explain: Misquoting or misrepresenting a creator's work damages its integrity and her reputation, which is protected by moral rights. Economic rights (D) are tempting, but no payment issue is described.

questions.stem: A musician sells the rights to her album to a record label. Which of the following statements is MOST accurate?
options: The label now holds both her economic and moral rights.
She loses all rights to the album permanently.
She keeps her moral rights, although the label now holds the economic rights.
She keeps the economic rights, but the label holds the moral rights.
questions.explain: Economic rights are generally transferable, while moral rights typically remain with the creator because they are tied to her personal reputation. Option A is tempting because she "sold the rights", but moral rights normally stay with the original creator.

questions.stem: Copyright is BEST defined as the legal right that
options: gives the creator of an original work control over how it is reproduced, distributed and used
allows anyone to copy a work once it is published online
lets a publisher change a work without the creator's consent
questions.explain: Copyright gives the creator control over reproduction, distribution and use of an original work. Option B is tempting because online material is easy to copy, but being online does not remove copyright protection.

questions.stem: In the copyright concept, which party enters into agreements with producers to record, film or print material and distribute it?
questions.explain: Publishers/distributors make agreements with producers to record, film or print and distribute work in ways that protect the producer's financial interests. Producers/owners (C) are tempting, but they create and own the work; they do not distribute it under agreement.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to reprint two chapters of a textbook for her class. According to the copyright concept, she should
options: retype the chapters so they are no longer the same document
photocopy them, because it is for education
acknowledge the source and seek permission from the publisher, who may charge a fee
use them without credit, as long as she does not sell them
questions.explain: As a consumer/user, she must acknowledge the source and seek permission through the publisher, who may charge a fee. Option B is tempting because the purpose is educational, but educational use does not automatically remove the need for permission.

questions.stem: Materials deliberately released for free use, adaptation and sharing, often under a Creative Commons licence, are known as
questions.explain: OERs are teaching, learning and research materials released for free use, adaptation and sharing. Source and turnaround documents (B, A) are tempting because they are EDPM terms, but they describe documents used in business processing, not openly licensed materials.

questions.stem: The MAIN purpose of a Creative Commons licence is to
options: transfer the creator's moral rights to the user
remove the need to credit the creator
prevent anyone from using a work
state exactly how a work may be used without the user contacting the creator
questions.explain: A Creative Commons licence sets out the conditions of use, such as whether the work may be modified or used commercially, so users do not need to ask permission directly. Option B is tempting because the work is free, but most Creative Commons licences require attribution.

questions.stem: A brochure that will be sold to tourists uses an image marked CC BY-NC. Which of the following BEST describes this use?
options: Acceptable, because the creator is credited
Not acceptable, because NC does not allow commercial use
Not acceptable, because CC images may never be printed
Acceptable, because all Creative Commons images are free
questions.explain: NC means non-commercial, so the image may not be used in a product that is sold. Option A is tempting because credit is required by BY, but crediting the creator does not override the non-commercial condition.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of protecting intellectual property for an ORGANISATION?
options: It guarantees the organisation will never be criticised.
It reduces legal risk and builds a reputation for ethical conduct.
It allows the organisation to copy competitors' work freely.
It removes the need for a reference list.
questions.explain: Respecting others' intellectual property and protecting its own reduces an organisation's legal risk and builds a reputation for ethical, professional conduct. Option A is tempting but overstated; protection reduces risk, it does not guarantee freedom from criticism.

questions.stem: Plagiarism is BEST described as
options: using another person's work without giving appropriate credit
quoting a source with quotation marks and a citation
using any source in a research project
questions.explain: Plagiarism is the use of another person's intellectual property without appropriate credit. Option C is tempting, but using sources is good research; it becomes plagiarism only when credit is missing.

questions.stem: A student changes a few words in each sentence of a website paragraph and does not name the website. This is
questions.explain: Close paraphrasing without acknowledgement is a form of plagiarism, because the ideas and structure still belong to the original author. Option B is tempting because some words were changed, but a real paraphrase rewrites thoroughly AND cites the source.

questions.stem: Shanice submits the essay she wrote for Business Studies last term as a new EDPM assignment, without telling her teacher. This is called
questions.explain: Reusing your own previously completed work without acknowledging that it has been used before is self-plagiarism. Some students think it cannot be plagiarism because the work is her own, but it misleads the evaluator into believing the work is new.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a guideline for avoiding plagiarism?
options: Acknowledging references in the text and in a bibliography or reference list
Submitting the same essay to two classes without mention
Paraphrasing without ever citing the source
questions.explain: Acknowledging references in text and in a bibliography or reference list is one of the syllabus guidelines. Option C is tempting because paraphrasing is a good skill, but a paraphrase must still be cited.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST reflects effective time management?
options: Starting an assignment the night before it is due
Doing the easiest tasks first and leaving the rest
Planning and prioritising tasks with enough time for review before the deadline
questions.explain: Effective time management means planning and prioritising realistically, allowing time for review and correction. Option B is tempting because it feels productive, but it ignores priorities and leaves important work to the last minute.

questions.stem: An assistant e-mails a contract to a client and the next morning phones to confirm it was received. This is an example of
questions.explain: Checking back to confirm that something sent was received is a follow-up procedure. Submission (C) is tempting because the contract was sent, but submission is the sending; the phone call afterwards is the follow-up.

questions.stem: Netiquette applies to online interactions via
options: e-mail, web forums, blogs, multiplayer gaming and social networking
questions.explain: Netiquette covers all online communication, including e-mail, web forums, blogs, multiplayer gaming and social networking. Option C is tempting because e-mail etiquette is common in offices, but netiquette is much wider.

questions.stem: Repeated, deliberate harm directed at another person online is called
questions.explain: Cyberbullying is repeated, deliberate harm directed at another person online. Netiquette (B) is tempting because it is about online behaviour, but netiquette is the set of rules for GOOD behaviour, the opposite of cyberbullying.

questions.stem: A student screenshots a friend's private message and posts it to the class group chat. Which netiquette rule has been broken?
questions.explain: Posting someone's private message without permission is unauthorised sharing of content. Cite sources (C) is tempting because the friend is "the source", but the issue is lack of permission, not lack of credit.

questions.stem: Completing tasks reliably and to standard, even when no one is directly overseeing the work, describes
questions.explain: Individual responsibility, or working without supervision, means completing work reliably without oversight. Willingness (B) is tempting, but willingness is the readiness to accept tasks without complaint, not how well they are completed alone.

questions.stem: Which desirable work attitude is MOST directly demonstrated by consistently arriving and delivering work on time?
questions.explain: Punctuality and regularity means arriving and delivering work on time consistently, not just occasionally. Team spirit (C) is tempting because punctual staff help the team, but the attitude described is specifically about timing and consistency.

questions.stem: Applying the same professionalism, punctuality and communication standards when working outside a traditional office describes
questions.explain: Remote working etiquette means keeping office standards when working from home or elsewhere, including virtual meeting conduct and prompt online communication. Individual responsibility (A) is tempting because remote work needs it, but the full description, including communication standards, defines remote working etiquette.

A smartwatch that counts your steps

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem:
The Portsmouth Marine Supplies has just computerised its stock and sales. Sort each statement from the staff meeting.

Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of computer usage?

The stock count that used to take two days now takes ten minutes.
questions.explain: Speed: computers complete in moments tasks that took people hours or days.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of computer usage?

A wrong price keyed in on Monday was charged to every customer all week.
questions.explain: Accuracy: garbage in, garbage out. The error was repeated accurately throughout the system.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of computer usage?

Five years of invoices now fit on one drive and can be searched by customer name.
questions.explain: Storage and retrieval: huge amounts in a small space, found almost instantly.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of computer usage?

A power cut during a storm shut down the tills for the afternoon.
questions.explain: Reliability: power outages undermine computer systems.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of computer usage?

Yacht owners in the lagoon can now order parts online at midnight.
questions.explain: E-commerce: the business can operate around the clock.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of computer usage?

A staff member clicked a fake "bank" e-mail and gave away the account password.
questions.explain: Cyber security: this is phishing.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem:
Is this an advantage or a disadvantage of computer usage?

The cashier's new adjustable chair and screen stand have ended her neck pain.
questions.explain: Ergonomics: well-designed equipment reduces physical strain.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem:

Some overseas customers do not trust paying a shop they have never visited.
questions.explain: E-commerce: building trust without face-to-face contact is a challenge.

questions.stem:
Your aunt runs the Sweet Soursop Bakery on King George V Street, Roseau. She wants to start taking orders online and asks for your advice. Make the best decisions.

Aunt Merle says: "If I sell online, I can stop worrying about anything going wrong. Computers never make mistakes." How do you respond?
options: "You are right. Once it is set up you never need to check it."
"Computers are very accurate, but only if the data is correct. If a price is typed wrongly, every order will be wrong. We should double-check what we enter."

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem: The online shop is ready. A week later, Aunt Merle gets an e-mail that looks like it is from her bank: "Your account is locked. Click here and enter your password." What do you advise?
options: "Click it quickly so the shop does not lose orders."
"Do not click the link. It may be phishing. Call the bank using the number on your card, and we will make sure the anti-virus and firewall are switched on."

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem: Some overseas customers are nervous about paying a small bakery they have never visited. How can the bakery build trust?
options: Add clear contact details, photos of the real shop, honest customer reviews and a secure, well-known payment method.
Ask customers to send cash by post first.

options: Files can be corrupted or lost without backups
Files take up little physical space

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem: A message pretending to be from a bank asking for your password is...
questions.explain: Phishing tricks people into revealing private details.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem: Which is an ADVANTAGE of e-commerce?
options: The business can operate around the clock
questions.explain: An online shop never closes; the other two are disadvantages.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage
questions.stem: Submitting a classmate's work as your own is an issue of...
questions.explain: Plagiarism is an ethical misuse of computers.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of computer usage

questions.explain: Software bugs, hardware failure and power outages undermine reliability.

options: In a shared cloud storage folder that all three of you can open.
On one CD-ROM that you pass around at school.
Only on your own laptop's hard disk.

questions.stem: The night before a storm is forecast, your teacher reminds the class to back up their SBA work. What do you do?
options: Nothing. It is in the cloud, so it can never be lost.
Copy the files onto a flash drive or portable hard disk as well, so there is a second copy in another location.

options: Take a short break, stretch your hands and look away from the screen, then adjust your chair and keyboard so your wrists stay straight.
Keep going without a break. The deadline is more important.

questions.topic: Caring for computers and factors associated with computer use
questions.stem: Your manager asks you to print all 300 pages of a draft report "just to read it through". What do you suggest?
options: Print three copies, just in case.
Proofread the draft on screen and print only the final, approved version.

questions.topic: Caring for computers and factors associated with computer use
questions.stem: The office is replacing five old monitors. What should happen to the old ones?
options: Leave them by the roadside with the household rubbish.
Arrange for them to be recycled responsibly, or donated if they still work.

questions.topic: Caring for computers and factors associated with computer use
questions.stem:
Name the factor or effect described in each statement.

Pain in the wrists after months of typing and using a mouse.
questions.explain: RSI comes from repeating the same movements for long periods.

questions.topic: Caring for computers and factors associated with computer use
questions.stem: A teenager who stays up late scrolling and cannot concentrate in class.
questions.explain: Excessive or poorly regulated use is linked to difficulty concentrating and disrupted sleep.

questions.topic: Caring for computers and factors associated with computer use

questions.explain: Computers make it easy to stay in touch with distant family.

questions.topic: Caring for computers and factors associated with computer use

questions.explain: Discarded devices create electronic waste.

questions.topic: Caring for computers and factors associated with computer use

questions.topic: Caring for computers and factors associated with computer use
questions.stem: Choosing a monitor with an energy-saving mode.
questions.explain: Energy-efficient equipment supports sustainable computer use.

Your partner is keying in a report in the computer lab. Sort each observation from your posture checklist.

Her feet are flat on the floor with her knees at about a right angle.
questions.explain: Correct position. A stable base keeps the back upright.

questions.stem:
Is this good or poor keyboarding posture?

Her wrists rest heavily on the edge of the desk while she types.
questions.explain: Wrists should hover just above the keys. Resting them bends the wrist and strains it.

questions.stem:
Is this good or poor keyboarding posture?

The top of the monitor is at, or slightly below, her eye level.
questions.explain: This is correct screen-to-eye-level contact and protects the neck.

questions.stem:
Is this good or poor keyboarding posture?

She leans forward with her arms stretched out to reach the keyboard.
questions.explain: The keyboard should be close enough that she does not stretch. Over-reaching strains the shoulders.

questions.stem:
Is this good or poor keyboarding posture?

Her shoulders are relaxed and her back is supported by the chair.
questions.explain: Relaxed shoulders and back support reduce tension during long sessions.

questions.stem:
Is this good or poor keyboarding posture?

The screen is only 20 cm from her face.
questions.explain: The screen should be about arm's length away to reduce eye strain.

questions.stem:
Is this good or poor keyboarding posture?

Her forearms are roughly parallel to the floor.
questions.explain: This shows the seat height is correct for the desk.

questions.stem:
Is this good or poor keyboarding posture?

Her chair is so low that her shoulders are raised to reach the keys.
questions.explain: Raised shoulders mean the seat is too low. Raise the chair until the forearms are level.

options: Lower the chair so her feet touch the floor.
Raise the chair until her forearms are level, and give her a footrest so her feet are supported.
Leave the chair as it is; she will get used to it.

questions.stem: The monitor sits on top of a filing box, so she has to tilt her head back to read. The desk faces the bright window. What now?
options: Make the screen brighter so she can see it over the sunlight.
Lower the monitor so the top is at or slightly below eye level, about arm's length away, and turn the desk at a right angle to the window.

questions.stem: The manager asks whether to spend the remaining budget on something to help her through an eight-hour day. Which do you recommend?
options: A sit-stand desk, so she can alternate between sitting and standing during the day.
A larger mouse mat with the company logo.

A special key such as Tab performs its action on its own, while a shortcut key such as Ctrl + C combines a modifier key with another key to perform a command.

questions.topic: Determining the Appropriate Software for a Task
questions.stem:
You are the student coordinator of the inter-school Twin-Island Youth Football Cup in St. Kitts and Nevis, with eight school teams. Make the best software decisions at each stage.

First you must keep the details of 160 players: name, school, date of birth, position and emergency contact. Coaches will ask questions such as "Which under-16 players from Sea-Almond Secondary School are goalkeepers?" What do you use?
options: Database management software, with a Players table and queries.
Graphic software, making a player poster.
A word processor, typing the players as a long list.

questions.topic: Determining the Appropriate Software for a Task
questions.stem: Next, you need a points table that updates goals, wins and points after every match and ranks the teams. What do you use?
options: Presentation software, retyping the table on a slide after each match.
A spreadsheet with formulas and sorting.

questions.topic: Determining the Appropriate Software for a Task
questions.stem: Finally, you must send a personalised letter to each of the 160 players' parents with the match schedule, and design a poster for the final. What do you do?
options: Mail merge in a word processor using the database as the data source, and design the poster in graphic software.
Type 160 separate letters by hand and draw the poster in the spreadsheet.

questions.stem: Ms. Hodge is preparing the Hummingbird Ridge High School newsletter and wants the body text in each column to meet both the left and right margins neatly. Which alignment should she use?

Keisha is formatting a business letter for Breedestraat Jewellers. Sort each formatting decision.

Is this formatting choice appropriate for a business letter?

Body text in Calibri 11 pt, black.
questions.explain: Legible, professional and in the standard 10 to 12 point range.

questions.stem:
Is this formatting choice appropriate for a business letter?

Each paragraph in a different decorative font to make it "interesting".
questions.explain: Decorative fonts and many fonts at once look amateurish. Use one or two professional fonts.

questions.stem:
Is this formatting choice appropriate for a business letter?

Single line spacing with one-inch margins.
questions.explain: This is the standard for business correspondence.

questions.stem:
Is this formatting choice appropriate for a business letter?

Every important word in bold, italics AND underline.
questions.explain: Emphasis loses its effect when overused. Bold should be used sparingly.

questions.stem:
Is this formatting choice appropriate for a business letter?

The shop's name in gold to match its logo.
questions.explain: Colour used purposefully and consistently for branding is appropriate.

questions.stem:
Is this formatting choice appropriate for a business letter?

A bright pink page background on the printed letter.
questions.explain: Backgrounds are generally for on-screen documents; they waste ink and look unprofessional on printed letters.

questions.stem:
Is this formatting choice appropriate for a business letter?

The © symbol inserted with the Symbol tool in the copyright line.
questions.explain: Symbols should be inserted with the software's symbol tool, not approximated.

questions.stem:
Is this formatting choice appropriate for a business letter?

A thick double border around every paragraph.
questions.explain: Borders should highlight key content only. Borders everywhere clutter the page.

questions.stem:
Shania works in the office of Grand Anse Tours. Choose the best technique for each task.

She must repeat the company's address at the top and bottom of a flyer, keeping the original.
questions.explain: Copy leaves the original in place and puts a duplicate on the clipboard.

questions.stem: Paragraph 4 of a report belongs on page 1.
questions.explain: Cut removes it from page 4 and paste inserts it on page 1. Copy would leave a duplicate behind.

questions.stem: The tour name "Sunset Cruise" must become "Twilight Cruise" in all 23 places in the brochure.
questions.explain: Find and Replace locates every occurrence and substitutes the new text automatically.

questions.stem: She has used the word "beautiful" five times in one paragraph.
questions.explain: The thesaurus suggests synonyms such as stunning or picturesque, avoiding repetition.

questions.stem: She wants to check whether the word "refund" appears anywhere in the terms and conditions.
questions.explain: A simple Search locates a word without changing anything.

questions.stem:
You are an office assistant at the Arnos Vale Insurance Agency. Your supervisor needs a 3-page letter to 40 clients by 3 p.m. It is 2.15 p.m.

The letter refers to the "2025 premium rates" eleven times. Your supervisor says they should all read "2026 premium rates". What do you do?
options: Use Find and Replace: find "2025 premium" and replace with "2026 premium", then check the results.
Scroll through and retype each one by hand.

questions.stem: Spelling check finishes with no errors. It is 2.40 p.m. What next?
options: Print immediately. Spell check found nothing, so it must be perfect.
Proofread quickly but carefully against the draft, paying special attention to figures and names.

questions.stem: You notice the policy number "SVG-4471" is wrong; it should be "SVG-4417". The cursor is in front of "4471". You want to fix it quickly.
options: Switch to type over mode and type 4417 over 4471, then switch back to insert mode.
Leave it. Nobody checks policy numbers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a SIMPLE tabulation skill, rather than an advanced one?
options: Applying borders and aligning a table on the page
Inserting a chart from table data
Using a spreadsheet formula to calculate totals automatically

questions.stem:
Five Form 4 students' EDPM test scores are in cells B2 to B6 of a spreadsheet: B2 = 72, B3 = 85, B4 = 64, B5 = 91, B6 = 78. Work out each result.

=SUM(B2:B6) returns...
=AVERAGE(B2:B6) returns...
questions.explain: 390 divided by 5 scores = 78.

questions.stem: =MIN(B2:B6) returns...
questions.explain: 64 is the smallest value in the range.

questions.stem: =MAX(B2:B6) returns...
questions.explain: 91 is the largest value in the range.

questions.stem: =B5-B4 returns...
questions.explain: 91 minus 64 = 27: the gap between the highest and lowest scores.

questions.stem: Which formula would find the highest score?
questions.explain: MAX returns the largest value. MIN is the tempting wrong answer because it also picks out one value, but it picks the smallest.

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem:
Ms. Ramdial is designing a table for the San Fernando Youth Steel Orchestra's members. Sort each field into its best data type.

Which data type suits this field?

First Name
questions.explain: Names are letters, so Text.

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem:
Which data type suits this field?

Phone (e.g. +1 876 555 0193)
questions.explain: Phone numbers contain symbols and spaces and are never calculated, so Text.

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem:
Which data type suits this field?

Monthly fee paid (Cg)
questions.explain: An amount of money you might total, so Currency (a kind of number).

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem:
Which data type suits this field?

Date joined
questions.explain: A date, so Date/Time. This lets you sort by date and find members who joined after a certain day.

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem:
Which data type suits this field?

Years of experience
questions.explain: A quantity you might average or compare, so Number.

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem:
Which data type suits this field?

Instrument played
questions.explain: Words such as "tenor pan", so Text.

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem:
Which data type suits this field?

Date of birth
questions.explain: A date, so Date/Time.

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem:
Which data type suits this field?

Section (e.g. 2A)
questions.explain: It mixes a digit and a letter and is not calculated, so Text.

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem: The office at Calabash Point Secondary wants a list of only the students in Form Class 4B from the student contact table. Which of the following BEST describes the query?
options: Type the criterion "4B" in the Student ID field of the query.
Delete all the records that are not in 4B.
Sort the table by Last Name in ascending order.
Type the criterion "4B" in the Form Class field of the query.

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem:
Your EDPM teacher asks you to build a simple database for the small classroom library so books can be tracked.

First you choose the fields. Which set do you pick?
options: Just one field called "Book details" holding everything in one sentence.
Title, Author, Publisher, Year, Pages, Colour of cover, Category, Shelf, Price, ISBN
Book ID, Title, Author, Category, Date Borrowed

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem: Now you set data types. What type do you give Date Borrowed?

questions.topic: Creating a database using a single table
questions.stem: The teacher wants a printout of all Fiction books. What do you do?
options: Create a query with "Fiction" as the criterion in the Category field, then a report titled "Fiction Books" from that query.
Print the whole table and highlight the fiction books with a marker.

questions.stem:
Tia is designing graphics for the Canefield Road Bakery. Sort each action into the enhancement method it uses.

Which method of enhancing images is this?

Changing a photo of bread to warm golden tones to match the bakery's brand colours.
questions.explain: Changing the colour tone is recolouring.

questions.stem:
Which method of enhancing images is this?

Dragging a corner handle so the logo fits the top corner of the menu.
questions.explain: Scaling proportionally to fit a space is resizing.

questions.stem:
Which method of enhancing images is this?

Adding the caption "Fresh every morning since 1998" under the photo.
questions.explain: A caption is text combined with an image.

questions.stem:
Which method of enhancing images is this?

Turning a picture of the shop grey-scale for a "then and now" display.
questions.explain: Grey-scale is a recolour option.

questions.stem:
Which method of enhancing images is this?

Setting the width to 5 cm with Lock aspect ratio ticked.
questions.explain: Changing size while keeping proportions is resizing.

questions.stem:
Which method of enhancing images is this?

Placing the title "Johnny Cake Saturday" across the top of a photo.
questions.explain: Text layered over an image is combining with text.

questions.stem:
Which method of enhancing images is this?

Adding a callout label with an arrow pointing to the guava tart.
questions.explain: A callout label is text combined with the image.

questions.stem: Andre has built a logo from a circle, a palm tree picture and a text box. He has grouped them. Now he needs to change only the wording in the text box. What should he do FIRST?
options: Delete the logo and start again.
Ungroup the objects, edit the text box, then group them again.

questions.stem:
Nadia is preparing a five-slide talk for the Sandbox Tree College Career Day on "Careers in Digital Media". Make the best choice each time.

Body text size for slides shown in the school hall:
questions.explain: Text must be readable from the back of the hall. 12 pt suits printed letters, not slides.

questions.stem: Her slide 3 has four full paragraphs. She should...
options: add an animation to every sentence
reduce it to a few key points and say the rest aloud
questions.explain: The presenter, not the slide, delivers the full explanation.

questions.stem: Transitions:
options: a different flashy transition on every slide
questions.explain: Consistent, subtle transitions look professional and do not distract.

questions.stem: Which graphic best supports "Jobs in digital media are growing"?
options: a cartoon of a smiling computer
a simple column chart of job numbers over five years
questions.explain: A relevant chart illustrates the point better than text or decoration. A line chart would also work for change over time.

questions.stem: She will talk in person and take questions. Slide timing should be...
questions.explain: Manual advance keeps the slides in step with her speech and questions. Automatic timing suits kiosks.

questions.topic: Integrating information to produce complete documents
questions.stem:
You volunteer in the office of the St. John's Youth Carnival Troupe in Antigua. You must send a thank-you letter to 120 sponsors and a report to the committee.

The sponsors' names, addresses and donation amounts are already in a spreadsheet. How will you produce the 120 letters?
options: Type 120 separate letters, copying each name and amount by hand.
Write one letter and mail merge it with the spreadsheet, using merge fields for name, address and donation.

questions.topic: Integrating information to produce complete documents
questions.stem: You preview the first letter. It reads: "Dear MrBrooks, thank you for your generous donation of NAf500." What do you do?
options: Add a space between «Title» and «LastName» and after "Cg", preview several more records, then finish.

questions.topic: Integrating information to produce complete documents
questions.stem: The committee report needs a chart of donations by month. The treasurer may still update the figures. How do you add the chart?
options: Draw a new chart by hand in the word processor using figures you remember.
Copy the chart from the spreadsheet and paste it into the report as a linked chart, then add a caption.

questions.topic: Integrating information to produce complete documents
questions.stem:
Choose the best answer for each integration situation.
