The Spanish Town Pharmacy wants address labels for 500 customers stored in its database. Best method:
options: mail merge to labels using the database as the data source
questions.explain: Mail merge works for labels and envelopes as well as letters.

questions.topic: Integrating information to produce complete documents
questions.stem: Mail merge is an example of...
options: integration of information from different software
questions.explain: It combines a word-processed document with data from a spreadsheet or database.

questions.topic: Integrating information to produce complete documents
questions.stem: A report will be emailed to a client who does not have your spreadsheet file. The chart should be...
questions.explain: An embedded chart travels inside the document; a linked chart needs the original file to update.

questions.topic: Integrating information to produce complete documents
questions.stem: Using spreadsheet figures directly in a report instead of retyping them reduces...
questions.explain: Data that is never retyped cannot be mistyped.

questions.topic: Integrating information to produce complete documents
questions.stem: After combining text, a table and a chart, the final check is for...
questions.explain: An integrated document should read as a single, coherent whole.

questions.stem: ITQ: Which of the following documents is BEST suited to landscape orientation rather than portrait?
options: A three-paragraph business letter to a customer
A one-page memo reminding staff about a fire drill
A sales table for a King George V Street jewellery store with twelve monthly columns
A two-page report on student attendance

questions.stem:
Ms. Brooks, office manager at Canefield Marine Supplies, is setting up a batch of documents. Decide the orientation of each.

Should this document be portrait or landscape?

A business letter to a customer in Guadeloupe
questions.explain: Letters are always portrait.

questions.stem:
Should this document be portrait or landscape?

A certificate of appreciation for a long-serving employee
questions.explain: Certificates are usually landscape, which gives room for a large, centred name and a decorative border.

questions.stem:
Should this document be portrait or landscape?

A memo about new opening hours
questions.explain: Memos are short text documents, so portrait.

questions.stem:
Should this document be portrait or landscape?

A stock table with 10 columns (item, code, supplier, cost, and so on)
questions.explain: Many columns need width, so landscape.

questions.stem:
Should this document be portrait or landscape?

A wide bar chart comparing sales in 12 months
questions.explain: Twelve bars and their labels fit better across a landscape page.

questions.stem:
Should this document be portrait or landscape?

The agenda for the monthly staff meeting
questions.explain: An agenda is a numbered list of items, which suits portrait.

questions.stem:
Should this document be portrait or landscape?

Minutes of a board meeting
questions.explain: Minutes are running text with numbered items, so portrait.

questions.stem:
You are the office assistant at the Roseau Travel Bureau. Choose the MOST appropriate stationery for each task.

ITQ: A one-line reminder to all staff that the office will close at noon on Friday.
questions.explain: It is internal, brief and goes to many staff, so a memo is the right choice. Letterhead is for external correspondence.

questions.stem: A letter confirming a hotel booking for a client in Curaçao.
questions.explain: External, official correspondence goes on letterhead so the client knows exactly who sent it.

questions.stem: Collecting each staff member's preferred vacation dates in the same format.
questions.explain: A form has fixed fields, so every answer comes back in a standard format.

questions.stem: Addressing 150 envelopes for a holiday mailing.
questions.explain: Mail-merged labels let you address many envelopes quickly and neatly.

questions.stem: Binding a 20-page tourism proposal for a meeting with a cruise line.
questions.explain: A document cover protects the proposal and makes it look professional.

questions.stem: Producing the same monthly newsletter layout every month.
questions.explain: A template keeps the layout and branding consistent each time.

questions.topic: Letterheads and the parts of a business letter
questions.stem:
These lines were taken from letters keyed in by Form 4 students. Sort each line by its punctuation style.

Which punctuation style does this line use?

Dear Sir
questions.explain: No comma after the salutation: open.

questions.topic: Letterheads and the parts of a business letter
questions.stem:
Which punctuation style does this line use?

Yours faithfully,
questions.explain: A comma after the close: closed.

questions.topic: Letterheads and the parts of a business letter
questions.stem:
Which punctuation style does this line use?

Kingston,
questions.explain: A comma at the end of an address line: closed.

questions.topic: Letterheads and the parts of a business letter
questions.stem:
Which punctuation style does this line use?

Mr J Hodge
questions.explain: No full stops after Mr or the initial: open.

questions.topic: Letterheads and the parts of a business letter
questions.stem:
Which punctuation style does this line use?

5th November, 2026.
questions.explain: Comma and full stop in the date: closed.

questions.topic: Letterheads and the parts of a business letter
questions.stem:
Which punctuation style does this line use?

5 November 2026
questions.explain: No punctuation in the date: open.

questions.topic: Letterheads and the parts of a business letter
questions.stem:
Which punctuation style does this line use?

Encs.
questions.explain: A full stop after the abbreviation: closed.

questions.topic: Letterheads and the parts of a business letter
questions.stem:
Which punctuation style does this line use?

Jamaica
questions.explain: The last address line has no full stop: open.

questions.topic: Letterheads and the parts of a business letter
questions.stem: A letter to the Caribbean Shipping Agency begins "Dear Sir or Madam" because the writer does not know who will read it. Which complimentary close is correct?

Mr Hodge, the EDPM teacher, describes letters on the classroom wall. Name the style of each.

Every line, including the date and "Yours faithfully", starts at the left margin.
questions.explain: Everything at the left margin is the definition of blocked.

questions.stem: The paragraphs start at the left margin, but the date and the close are tabbed toward the right.
questions.explain: Blocked paragraphs plus a right-positioned date and close = semi-blocked.

questions.stem: The first line of each paragraph is indented, and the date sits on the right.
questions.explain: Indented first lines are the feature that marks the indented style.

questions.stem: Which style is quickest to key in, because you never need tab stops for the date or close?
questions.explain: In blocked style everything starts at the left margin, so no tabs are needed.

questions.stem: Which punctuation style is MOST often paired with a blocked letter?
questions.explain: Blocked letters usually use open punctuation. Full is another name for closed.

questions.stem: ITQ: Which statement gives ONE correct similarity and ONE correct difference between a blocked letter and a semi-blocked letter?
options: Both begin paragraphs at the left margin; in the semi-blocked letter the date and close are positioned toward the right.
Both place the date on the right; only the blocked letter has an inside address.
Both must use closed punctuation; only the semi-blocked letter has a subject heading.
Both indent the first line of every paragraph; only the blocked letter has a date.

questions.stem:
You work at Pelican Construction in Chaguanas. Your manager has drafted a long letter to the Ministry about a building project, and it will not fit on one page. Make the right production decisions.

The letter runs about a third of the way onto a second page. What paper do you use for page 2?
options: Another sheet of letterhead, so it matches.
Plain paper of the same size and quality as the letterhead.

questions.stem: What do you put at the top of page 2?
options: The full letterhead and the inside address again.
The page number, the date and the recipient's name.
Nothing. The reader will know it continues.

questions.stem: When you check Print Preview, page 2 contains only "Yours faithfully" and the signature block. What do you do?
options: Insert a page break before the last paragraph so that at least two or three body lines move to page 2 with the closing.
Leave it. The letter is complete.

questions.stem: ITQ: Which statement BEST explains the difference in purpose between the notations CONFIDENTIAL and URGENT?
options: CONFIDENTIAL is for letters; URGENT is for envelopes only.
CONFIDENTIAL is used only by the government; URGENT is used by businesses.
CONFIDENTIAL controls WHO may open the item; URGENT controls HOW QUICKLY it should be dealt with.
They mean the same thing; URGENT is simply stronger.

questions.stem:
You are the administrative assistant in the Human Resources office of the Caribbean Harbour Services in Belmopan. Three letters must go out today. Choose the correct handling.

Letter 1 tells an employee the result of a disciplinary hearing. It will go to her office, where a secretary opens the mail. What notation do you use?
options: CONFIDENTIAL, on the letter above the inside address AND on the envelope.

questions.stem: Letter 2 is to a supplier and must reach him today because a contract deadline is tomorrow. The contents are routine. What do you add?
options: URGENT (and BY HAND if it is delivered by messenger).

questions.stem: Letter 3 is the manager's personal letter to a staff member congratulating her on her wedding. Which notation fits best?
options: PERSONAL, because it concerns her as an individual, not her job.
CONFIDENTIAL, because all HR letters are confidential.

questions.stem:
Choose the BEST expansion of each skeleton note for a formal document.

"pls confirm attendance by Fri"
options: Please confirm your attendance by Friday 6 November.
questions.explain: It expands the abbreviations, forms a complete polite sentence and adds the exact date.

questions.stem: "order recd - thanks - delivery wk of 9th"
options: Thank you for your order, which we have received. Delivery will be made during the week beginning 9 November.
We got the order and it will come soon.
questions.explain: Complete, formal sentences that keep the precise meaning (the week beginning the 9th).

questions.stem: Voice message: "Um, tell the Form 5s the trip's moved to, like, the 20th."
options: The Form 5 field trip has been rescheduled to Friday 20 November.
The Form 5 trip has been cancelled.
Um, the Form 5 trip is moved to like the 20th.
questions.explain: Fillers are removed, the tone is formal and the meaning (rescheduled, not cancelled) is kept.

questions.stem: "remind all staff - ID badges must be worn at all times"
options: Some staff might want to wear their badges.
All staff are reminded that identification badges must be worn at all times.
questions.explain: It keeps the instruction's strength ("must") and expands ID to identification.

questions.stem: "cost approx Cg 2,500 incl VAT"
options: The cost is approximately Cg 2,500, including turnover tax.
The cost is approximately Cg 2,500, including VAT.
questions.explain: Expand approx and incl, but do not change what the writer said. If the notes say VAT, keep VAT unless you are told to correct it; changing the tax name changes the meaning.

questions.stem:
ITQ: Sort each feature into the document it belongs to.

Is this a feature of a business letter or a memo?

Sent to people inside the organisation
questions.explain: Memos are for internal communication.

questions.stem:
Is this a feature of a business letter or a memo?

Has an inside address
questions.explain: Letters carry the recipient's full address. Memos do not.

questions.stem:
Is this a feature of a business letter or a memo?

Opens with TO, FROM, DATE and SUBJECT
questions.explain: This heading block is the mark of a memo.

questions.stem:
Is this a feature of a business letter or a memo?

Ends with "Yours faithfully" or "Yours sincerely"
questions.explain: The complimentary close belongs to letters only.

questions.stem:
Is this a feature of a business letter or a memo?

Printed on letterhead for external readers
questions.explain: Letterhead is for external correspondence.

questions.stem:
Is this a feature of a business letter or a memo?

May end with the sender's initials instead of a signature
questions.explain: Memos often end with the sender's initials.

questions.stem:
Is this a feature of a business letter or a memo?

Begins with a salutation such as "Dear Mr Gumbs"
questions.explain: Memos have no salutation.

questions.stem:
Is this a feature of a business letter or a memo?

Headings aligned with tab stops at the top
questions.explain: The TO/FROM/DATE/SUBJECT labels are aligned with tab stops.

questions.stem: A memo from the Bay Street Pharmacy manager has the standard heading, then four paragraphs under the side headings "Background", "New Procedure", "Training" and "Action Required". Every line starts at the left margin. This memo is BEST described as a

You have just been elected secretary of the Seagrape Bay Secondary School Environmental Club. The first committee meeting is in two weeks. Make the right decisions.

The chairperson asks you to let members know about the meeting. What do you prepare first?
options: The minutes, so they are ready.
A notice of meeting with the date, time, venue and purpose, together with the agenda, sent to all members in advance.

questions.stem: The chairperson asks for something to help her run the meeting. What do you give her?
options: A chairman's agenda: each item with background notes on the left and a blank NOTES column on the right.
A copy of the ordinary agenda, the same as everyone else's.

questions.stem: The meeting is over. The club agreed to hold a beach clean-up at Junkanoo Beach, and three members volunteered for tasks. What do you produce?
options: Minutes in the past tense and reported speech, plus an action items list showing each task, the person responsible and the due date.
A memo saying "Good meeting. See you at the beach."

questions.stem:
Tamara is adding graphics to the Business Club's end-of-term report. Choose the best action each time.

Her photo of the club stall looks stretched and squashed.
options: She should make it behind text.
She resized it by dragging a side handle; she should use a corner handle.
questions.explain: Corner handles keep the proportions (aspect ratio). Side handles stretch the picture.

questions.stem: A small logo should sit beside the first paragraph with text flowing around it.
questions.explain: Square wrapping lets the paragraph flow around the logo's box.

questions.stem: A wide bar chart of sales should have text above and below, not beside it.
questions.explain: Top and bottom keeps the text clear of the sides of a wide chart.

questions.stem: The chart about fundraising has been placed on the last page, two pages after the paragraph that discusses it.
options: Leave it; readers can find it.
Move it as close as possible to the paragraph it relates to.
questions.explain: Readers should be able to connect the graphic with the text immediately.

questions.stem: Readers do not know what the chart shows.
options: Add a caption such as "Figure 1: Funds raised by month".
questions.explain: A caption explains what the graphic shows.

questions.stem: The Examinations Officer at Mahoe Grove High School is preparing the CSEC mock timetable for 14 subjects across 10 days, with columns for date, time, subject, paper and room. Which of the following is the BEST choice, and why?
options: Ruled work, because rules between rows and columns help readers track a large amount of tabulated information accurately.
Unruled work, because tab stops cannot be used with tables.
Unruled work, because lines make any document look old-fashioned.
Centred/displayed work, because every line should be centred on the page.

questions.stem:
Island Fresh Supermarket, English Harbour, has this organisation chart. Level 1: General Manager. Level 2: Store Manager, Accounts Manager. Level 3 under the Store Manager: Head Cashier, Stock Supervisor. Level 3 under the Accounts Manager: Accounts Clerk. Answer each question.

How many levels of hierarchy does the chart show?
questions.explain: There are three rows: General Manager; the two managers; then the clerk, cashier and supervisor.

questions.stem: To whom does the Stock Supervisor report?
questions.explain: The Stock Supervisor sits on level 3 under the Store Manager, joined by a vertical line.

questions.stem: The Store Manager and the Accounts Manager should be drawn...
options: on the same row, in boxes of the same size
questions.explain: They are at the same level, so they share a row and a box size.

questions.stem: Which position belongs in the single box at the top?
questions.explain: The most senior position always sits at the top, centred.

questions.stem: Which tool in Word builds this chart most quickly?
questions.explain: The SmartArt Hierarchy layouts are designed for organisation charts.

questions.stem:
You are the office assistant at Bayside Hardware, St. John’s. The manager asks you to prepare the Third Quarter Sales Report (July to September) with a sales chart from the company spreadsheet. Make the best decisions.

The report will be printed, signed by the manager and filed as the official record of the third quarter. The sales spreadsheet is updated every day. How do you insert the chart?
options: As an embedded graph, so the report keeps the Q3 figures exactly as they stood when the quarter closed.
As a linked graph, because linked graphs are always better.

questions.stem: Before inserting, you notice the spreadsheet still shows two September sales that were cancelled. What do you do?
options: Insert the chart anyway. Embedded graphs can be fixed later by editing the spreadsheet.
Ask the accounts clerk to correct the spreadsheet first, then create the embedded chart from the corrected figures.

questions.stem: The manager also wants a one-page sales dashboard for the staffroom notice board, reprinted every Monday with the latest figures. How should that chart be inserted?
options: As a linked graph, with the spreadsheet kept in the same shared folder so the link does not break.
As an embedded graph, rebuilt from scratch every Monday.

questions.stem:
Your group is producing a 4-page A5 leaflet (one A4 sheet folded once) for the Breadfruit Valley Secondary Science Fair (Activity 3). Sort each piece of content to the side of the sheet where it is printed.

Which side of the A4 sheet?

The title "Science Fair 2026" with a large photo
questions.explain: The title goes on page 1, the front cover, which is on the outside.

questions.stem:
Which side of the A4 sheet?

Map of the school and contact telephone number
questions.explain: Contact details and maps usually go on page 4, the back cover, which is also on the outside.

questions.stem:
Which side of the A4 sheet?

Welcome message from the Principal
questions.explain: The welcome is the first thing you read inside, on page 2.

questions.stem:
Which side of the A4 sheet?

List of the projects and their room numbers
questions.explain: The main content belongs on the inside pages, 2 and 3.

questions.stem:
Which side of the A4 sheet?

Timetable of judging and prize-giving
questions.explain: Detailed content sits on the inside spread.

questions.stem:
Which side of the A4 sheet?

Sponsors' logos and a thank-you line
questions.explain: Acknowledgements commonly go on the back cover.

questions.stem: In a press release, the opening (lead) paragraph should typically answer...
options: who, what, when, where and why
only the price of the product

questions.stem:
You work in the office of Island Events, Frigate Bay, St. Kitts. Your manager hands you a handwritten draft of a services agreement with a new client and asks you to key it in. Make the best decisions.

The draft says: "Agreement btwn Island Events & Mr. T. Carty, dep. $500 due 3/4/26." How do you key the opening and the deposit clause?
options: Ask the manager for Mr. Carty's full legal name and confirm the date, then key: "THIS AGREEMENT is made between ISLAND EVENTS and TREVOR JAMES CARTY ... a deposit of five hundred United States dollars (US$500.00) shall be paid on or before the third day of April, two thousand and twenty-six."
Exactly as written, to save time.

questions.stem: The draft has six terms written as one long paragraph. How do you set them out?
options: As a bulleted list with coloured bullets.
As numbered clauses (1, 2, 3 ... with 2.1, 2.2 for sub-points).

questions.stem: You have finished keying. What do you do before handing it to the manager?
options: Proofread line by line against the draft, checking every name, date and figure (ideally reading aloud with a colleague), and add a signature block for both parties and a witness.
Run the spell checker only. It will catch any mistakes.

questions.stem:
Bodden Town Builders in Grand Cayman is preparing a bill of quantity to repair the roof of a community centre after a storm. Answer each question.

Item 1: 45 galvanised roof sheets at US$28.00 each. The amount is...
questions.explain: 45 x 28.00 = 1,260.00. Amount = Quantity x Rate.

questions.stem: Item 2: 12 boxes of roofing screws at US$15.50 per box. The amount is...
Item 3: 24 hours of labour at US$40.00 per hour. The amount is...
The total of Items 1 to 3 is...
How should the figures in the Amount column be aligned?
questions.explain: Right or decimal alignment keeps the units, tens and decimal points in line so the column can be checked and added.

questions.stem:
A construction company in the Cayman Islands produces many documents for one project. Sort each document.

Is this a legal or a technical document?

The signed building contract with a penalty for late completion
questions.explain: A contract sets out binding obligations and consequences: legal.

questions.stem:
Is this a legal or a technical document?

An itemised list of blocks, cement and labour hours with rates
questions.explain: That is a bill of quantity: technical.

questions.stem:
Is this a legal or a technical document?

The architect's description of the concrete mix and roof fixings to be used
questions.explain: That is a specification: technical.

questions.stem:
Is this a legal or a technical document?

The deed transferring the land from the vendor to the client
questions.explain: A conveyance document transfers ownership: legal.

questions.stem:
Is this a legal or a technical document?

A list of exactly what work is and is not included in the project
questions.explain: That is a scope of works: technical.

questions.stem:
Is this a legal or a technical document?

An amendment adding storm cover to the site's insurance policy
questions.explain: An endorsement modifies an existing policy: legal.

questions.stem:
Is this a legal or a technical document?

The lease for the temporary storage yard
questions.explain: A lease grants use of property for rent: legal.

questions.stem:
The Drama Club is preparing scripts for three productions. Sort each script feature into the medium it belongs to MOST.

Which script would this line appear in?

SFX: THUNDER ROLLS. RAIN BEATS ON A GALVANISE ROOF.
questions.explain: Detailed sound cues let a radio audience "see" the scene through sound.

questions.stem:
Which script would this line appear in?

MUSIC: STEEL PAN FADES IN, THEN UNDER.
questions.explain: Music cues on their own line are a radio convention.

questions.stem:
Which script would this line appear in?

(She walks downstage and sits on the bench, facing the audience.)
questions.explain: "Downstage", "facing the audience": a stage direction for theatre.

questions.stem:
Which script would this line appear in?

ACT TWO, SCENE ONE. The verandah of an old house in Soufrière.
questions.explain: Act and scene headings with a set description are theatre conventions.

questions.stem:
Which script would this line appear in?

EXT. NEGRIL BEACH – DAY
questions.explain: A scene heading with EXT. and a time of day is a television (screen) convention.

questions.stem:
Which script would this line appear in?

CLOSE-UP on the letter in his shaking hand.
questions.explain: Camera directions belong to television scripts.

questions.stem:
Which script would this line appear in?

CUT TO:
questions.explain: A transition between camera shots: television.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST distinguishes a profit and loss statement from a balance sheet?
options: A profit and loss statement summarises income and expenses over a period to show profit or loss; a balance sheet shows assets, liabilities and owner's equity at a specific point in time.
A balance sheet is used only by non-profit organisations; a profit and loss statement is used only by banks.
A profit and loss statement lists every bank transaction; a balance sheet lists every invoice.
They are the same document with different names.

questions.stem:
Kim's Kitchen catered a christening for Mrs. A. Lake: 40 meal boxes at US$15.00 each, 40 drinks at US$2.50 each, and a delivery charge of US$25.00. Mrs. Lake paid a deposit of US$200.00. Answer each question.

The amount for the 40 meal boxes is...
The amount for the 40 drinks is...
The invoice total, including delivery, is...
After the deposit, the balance due is...
The document Kim gives Mrs. Lake when she pays the balance is a(n)...
questions.explain: A receipt confirms payment has been made. The invoice asked for the payment.

questions.stem: Which detail must appear on every invoice so it can be traced later?
questions.explain: A unique, sequential invoice number lets both the seller and the customer trace and file the document.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes creating a template WITHOUT a wizard?
options: Copying a completed document and deleting its content.
Printing a document without saving it.
Building the layout and formatting manually from a blank document, then saving it as a template file type.
Using a step-by-step prompt that asks for your company name and generates a document automatically.

questions.stem:
You are the office administrator at Caribbean Vows. A new couple has just booked a wedding at a hotel on Grand Turk. Choose the right document at each stage.

The couple has agreed to the Gold Package. Before any work starts, the business needs their commitment in writing, with both parties' obligations and a cancellation clause. What do you prepare?
options: A friendly flyer listing the Gold Package features.
A services agreement with numbered clauses, the couple's full legal names, the fee in words and figures, and a signature block for both parties and a witness.

questions.stem: The hotel's decor contractor needs to know exactly what Caribbean Vows will supply and what the hotel will supply, with quantities of chairs, linens and flowers. What do you prepare?
options: An organisation chart of the business.
A scope of works (what is and is not included) and a bill of quantity (items, quantities, rates, amounts).

questions.stem: This is the fourth wedding this month and you are formatting the invoice from a blank page again. The last one had a wrong address. What do you do?
options: Open last month's invoice, type over the details and save it with the same name.
Build an invoice template with the logo, table, formulas and placeholders, save it as a template file type, and use it for every new client.

questions.stem:
Each card describes something happening at Harbour Street Jewels head office. Sort it into the correct group.

Which group of electronic communication is this?

The sales team publishes a weekly written post about new jewellery designs.
questions.explain: A regularly updated written post is a weblog (blog), which is a form of social media.

questions.stem:
Which group of electronic communication is this?

Staff record a monthly audio episode about caring for gold and silver.
questions.explain: An episodic audio programme is a podcast, which the syllabus lists under social media.

questions.stem:
Which group of electronic communication is this?

Customers post questions on an online discussion board about watch repairs.
questions.explain: A discussion board on a specific topic is an Internet forum, a form of social media.

questions.stem:
Which group of electronic communication is this?

The clerk sends a signed customs form over the telephone line to the broker.
questions.explain: Transmitting a scanned document over a telephone line is a facsimile (fax).

questions.stem:
Which group of electronic communication is this?

One machine in the corner prints, copies, scans and faxes.
questions.explain: A machine that combines several office functions is a multifunctional device.

questions.stem:
Which group of electronic communication is this?

A receipt is scanned and saved straight into the Accounts folder.
questions.explain: Saving the scan to a folder is scan to file, a multifunctional device feature.

questions.stem:
Which group of electronic communication is this?

The manager sends a written message with a price list attached to a supplier in Miami.
questions.explain: A written message with an attachment sent over the internet is e-mail.

questions.stem:
Which group of electronic communication is this?

The assistant looks up a shipping company's rates on its website.
questions.explain: Browsing linked pages and online services is using the World Wide Web.

questions.stem:
At Pelican Bay Medical Centre, the receptionist has 60 paper patient-registration forms from this week. The forms must be kept on the centre's shared drive so that any authorised staff member can find them later. Nobody needs to receive them today.

Which feature of the multifunctional device is MOST suitable for this task?
options: Fax, sending the forms to the centre's own fax number
Scan to mail, sending each form to the doctor's inbox
Copy, making a second paper set for the filing cabinet
Scan to file, saving the forms in a named folder on the shared drive

questions.stem:
You are the office assistant at Palmetto Point Secondary. For each person, choose the correct field.

The Head of Department must approve the Form 5 exam timetable you are sending.
questions.explain: She is expected to act (approve), so she is a primary, direct recipient in To.

questions.stem: The principal should be kept informed about the timetable but does not need to reply.
questions.explain: Cc is for people who should be kept informed but are not expected to act.

questions.stem: You are sending a fundraising thank-you to 120 parents who do not know each other.
questions.explain: Bcc hides each parent's address from the others, protecting their privacy.

questions.stem: Which field lets ALL recipients see who else received the message?
questions.explain: Addresses in To and Cc are visible to all recipients. Only Bcc addresses are hidden.

questions.stem: The bus company must confirm it can transport the netball team on Saturday.
questions.explain: The bus company must act (confirm), so it goes in To.

questions.stem: The PE teacher should know the bus has been booked, but has nothing to do.
questions.explain: She only needs to be informed, so Cc is correct.

questions.stem: A manager needs to send the same announcement to 40 clients who do not know each other, without revealing their e-mail addresses to one another. Which feature should be used?
options: Paste the 40 addresses into the subject line.
Put all 40 addresses in the To field.
Put all 40 addresses in the Cc field.
Put all 40 addresses in the Bcc field.

questions.stem:
You are the student secretary of the Bayleaf Hill Secondary Business Club. You must e-mail the 35 local businesses that donated prizes for the school fair, thanking them and attaching the photo report. Your teacher, the club adviser, wants a copy.

You open a new message. How do you address it?
options: Put all 35 businesses and your teacher in To.
Put your own address in To, the 35 businesses in Bcc, and your teacher in Cc.

questions.stem: Now the subject line. Which one do you type?
options: Thank you for supporting the BHS school fair: photo report attached

questions.stem: The photo report is on your desktop as Document7.docx and also as SMA_Fair_Photo_Report_2026.pdf. Which do you attach?
options: Document7.docx, the first one you see.
Open and check SMA_Fair_Photo_Report_2026.pdf, then attach it and mention it in the message.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem:
Each card describes something that happened at Caribbean Courier Services office in Roseau. Sort it.

Does this show an advantage or a disadvantage of electronic communication?

A quotation reaches a client in Curaçao eight seconds after it is sent.
questions.explain: This is speed of delivery.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem:
Does this show an advantage or a disadvantage of electronic communication?

The manager sends one holiday-hours notice to 300 customers at once.
questions.explain: This is sending information to multiple recipients simultaneously.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem:
Does this show an advantage or a disadvantage of electronic communication?

Sending the monthly newsletter by e-mail saves the cost of paper and postage.
questions.explain: This is the cost advantage.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem:
Does this show an advantage or a disadvantage of electronic communication?

A payroll file is sent to "Kim Ross" instead of "Kim Roberts" because of auto-complete.
questions.explain: A message sent to the wrong address is an error in dispatch.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem:
Does this show an advantage or a disadvantage of electronic communication?

An urgent customs notice lands in the client's junk folder and is not seen for four days.
questions.explain: This is a challenge ensuring the message is received.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem:
Does this show an advantage or a disadvantage of electronic communication?

The clerk attaches last year's price list instead of this year's.
questions.explain: An incorrect attachment is also an error in dispatch.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem:
Does this show an advantage or a disadvantage of electronic communication?

The sender has no way of knowing whether the client actually read the delivery notice.
questions.explain: Uncertainty about whether the message was seen is a challenge ensuring it is received.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem:
It is 4:30 p.m. on the day before Emancipation Day. You are the administrator at Morvant Construction. You must send a signed contract to a client, Mr. Hodge, before the office closes.

You have two files in the folder: Contract_Hodge_draft.docx and Contract_Hodge_SIGNED.pdf. You are in a hurry. What do you do?
options: Attach the first file in the folder. There is no time to check.
Open the signed PDF to check it, then attach it.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem: You type "Ho" in the To field and auto-complete offers m.hodge@... and m.hodges@.... What do you do?
options: Pick the first one. They look the same.
Check the address against the client's file before selecting it.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem: The e-mail is sent at 4:45 p.m. The office reopens in two days. What now?
options: Call or message Mr. Hodge to say the contract has been sent and ask him to confirm receipt.
Go home. It was sent, so it must have arrived.

questions.topic: Advantages and disadvantages of electronic communication media
questions.stem: Which of the following BEST explains why speed of delivery can indirectly cause errors in dispatch?
options: Because sending is instant and easy, users may rush and skip checking addresses and attachments, and a sent message cannot be fully recalled.
Fast messages cost more to send than slow ones.
Fast messages are more likely to be filtered into the spam folder.
Speed means the message reaches too many recipients at once.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem:
For each workplace situation, choose the new or emerging technology that fits BEST.

A cooking school wants to show, step by step, how to make guava berry tarts.
questions.explain: Instructions that are best shown rely on visual and spoken communication, which is the key feature of vlogging.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem: A lawyer wants detailed, searchable articles on new rental laws that clients can find later.
questions.explain: Longer-form, text-based, searchable posts are the key feature of blogging.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem: A sales representative visiting hotels needs to call, e-mail and check stock from the road.
questions.explain: A smartphone combines many channels in one portable, always-connected device.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem: A recruitment officer wants to keep in touch with professional contacts and share company news.
questions.explain: Building and maintaining professional connections is the core use of social networking services.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem: Which of these makes a blog a REFLECTIVE technology?
options: Readers can comment and the writer can reply.
questions.explain: Reflective technologies allow the audience to respond and interact, not just receive.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem:
Sort each description by the type of communication it mainly relies on.

What does this mainly rely on?

A weekly 800-word post on budgeting tips for young workers.
questions.explain: Longer-form written posts are text-based, like blogging.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem:
What does this mainly rely on?

A posted review of a new tablet, written with headings and organised by category.
questions.explain: Written, searchable and organised by category: text-based.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem:
What does this mainly rely on?

A five-minute video tour of a new hotel room in Grace Bay.
questions.explain: Showing and speaking on camera is video-based, like vlogging.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem:
What does this mainly rely on?

A recorded on-camera tutorial on setting up a shop till.
questions.explain: Instructional video content is vlogging.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem:
What does this mainly rely on?

Calling a client, then checking e-mail and a map app on the same device.
questions.explain: Many communication channels in one portable device: a smartphone.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem:
What does this mainly rely on?

Sending a text, joining a video call and browsing a supplier's website while at the port.
questions.explain: Combining several channels from virtually any location is the key feature of a smartphone.

questions.topic: Comparing new and emerging communication technologies
questions.stem: Which of the following BEST compares blogging and vlogging?
options: Blogging is a device, whereas vlogging is a platform.
Blogging is text-based and searchable, whereas vlogging is video-based and relies on visual and spoken communication.
Vlogging is only for personal diaries, whereas blogging is only for businesses.
Both are one-way broadcast technologies that do not allow responses.

questions.topic: File organisation methods for sorting and storing e-mail
questions.stem:
You manage the inbox at Grand Anse Auto Parts. Choose the MOST useful sorting method for each task.

Find every e-mail exchanged with the supplier Caribe Tyres over the past year. (ITQ4)
questions.explain: Sorting by sender groups all the supplier's messages together, whatever their date or topic.

questions.topic: File organisation methods for sorting and storing e-mail
questions.stem: See which messages arrived since you left work yesterday.
questions.explain: Chronological order shows the most recent correspondence first.

questions.topic: File organisation methods for sorting and storing e-mail
questions.stem: Follow the whole conversation about "Warehouse shelving project" from the first quote to the final invoice.
questions.explain: Grouping by subject keeps the whole thread or project together from start to finish.

questions.topic: File organisation methods for sorting and storing e-mail
questions.stem: Work out the order of events in a delivery dispute: who wrote what, and when.
questions.explain: Reviewing a sequence of events over time calls for sorting by date.

questions.topic: File organisation methods for sorting and storing e-mail
questions.stem: Review everything your manager has sent you this term before your appraisal.
questions.explain: All correspondence from one colleague: sort by sender.

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem:
You are the personal assistant to the general manager of Bayside Resort & Marina in Antigua. Several decisions about how to communicate land on your desk in one morning.

At 10:00 a.m. you learn that a guest's credit card details may have been exposed. The manager is at a conference in Miami (at most one hour behind Antigua) and must know now. How do you tell him?
options: Post a note in the staff group chat.

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem: The manager asks you to inform the resort's 600 past guests of a routine change to the pool opening hours. Which medium do you choose?
options: Phone all 600 guests one by one.
A bulk, mail-merged e-mail, with addresses protected.

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem: New lifeguards need to learn the steps for using the pool rescue hoist. How do you communicate this?
options: A short video or diagram-based guide they can watch and review.
A long paragraph in an e-mail.

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem: A company must inform 200 customers, located across several time zones, about a routine change to its opening hours. Which medium is MOST appropriate?
options: An urgent SMS sent at midnight
A bulk e-mail sent to all customers using Bcc or mail merge
A phone call to each customer during the company's office hours
A face-to-face meeting with each customer

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem:
Sort each workplace habit.

Does this follow netiquette and safe practice?

Replying "Received, I will respond fully by Friday" to an important request.
questions.explain: Acknowledging receipt even when a full reply will take longer is good netiquette.

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem:
Does this follow netiquette and safe practice?

Proofreading a message before clicking Send.
questions.explain: Messages are hard to retract once sent, so proofreading is essential.

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem:
Does this follow netiquette and safe practice?

Calling the bank on its official number to check an e-mail that asks you to "verify your account".
questions.explain: Verifying unfamiliar or suspicious senders protects against fraud.

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem:
Does this follow netiquette and safe practice?

Forwarding a colleague's private message to the whole department.
questions.explain: This breaks privacy. Messages can spread far beyond their original audience.

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem:
Does this follow netiquette and safe practice?

Opening an attachment called "invoice.exe" from an unknown sender.
questions.explain: Suspicious attachments may contain malware.

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem:
Does this follow netiquette and safe practice?

Sharing a photographer's images in a company newsletter without permission or credit.
questions.explain: This does not respect intellectual property.

questions.topic: Selecting communication media, netiquette and safe online communication
questions.stem:
Does this follow netiquette and safe practice?

Leaving a client's important e-mail unanswered for three weeks.
questions.explain: Respond within a reasonable time, or at least acknowledge receipt.

questions.stem:
The Bayside Realty office in Gros Islet uses both systems. Sort each description into the system it describes.

Which filing system does this describe?

Lease agreements are kept in labelled folders in a four-drawer cabinet.
questions.explain: Folders in a cabinet are physical storage, so this is manual filing.

questions.stem:
Which filing system does this describe?

A clerk finds every 2025 lease in seconds by typing "2025 lease" in a search box.
questions.explain: Searching by keyword is a feature of electronic filing.

questions.stem:
Which filing system does this describe?

A copy for the owner has to be made on the photocopier.
questions.explain: Duplicating paper records requires physical photocopying.

questions.stem:
Which filing system does this describe?

Files sync automatically to the cloud every evening.
questions.explain: Automatic syncing and backup are electronic features.

questions.stem:
Which filing system does this describe?

Termites have damaged a box of old property records.
questions.explain: Pests are a risk to paper records.

questions.stem:
Which filing system does this describe?

Access is controlled by user accounts and passwords.
questions.explain: Passwords and permissions secure electronic files. Paper relies on locks and supervision.

questions.stem:
Which filing system does this describe?

A floor plan is e-mailed to a buyer in Curacao in seconds.
questions.explain: Instant sharing across locations is an electronic advantage.

questions.stem:
Which filing system does this describe?

The records room needs more space every year.
questions.explain: Manual systems need more physical space as records grow.

questions.stem:
Mrs. Hodge runs the Hodge Family Pharmacy on Bridge Street. Decide what each statement shows.

During a power cut, staff still find prescriptions in the paper file. This is...
questions.explain: Manual filing does not depend on electricity, so it keeps working in a power cut.

questions.stem: A virus deletes the stock records on the office computer. This is...
questions.explain: Electronic files are vulnerable to cyberattacks and malicious software.

questions.stem: The new assistant needs a week of training to use the filing software. This is...
questions.explain: Electronic systems need user training and technical maintenance.

questions.stem: Mrs. Hodge e-mails a supplier's invoice to her accountant in Rodney Bay instantly. This is...
questions.explain: Simple, instant remote sharing is an electronic advantage.

questions.stem: Finding a three-year-old receipt in the boxes takes the whole afternoon. This is...
questions.explain: Manual searching is slow and limited by how the papers were filed.

questions.stem: The Rodney Bay Law Chambers stores almost everything electronically. Which document is it MOST likely to keep in a manual (paper) file as well, and why?
options: A draft letter, because drafts are always more important than final copies.
The original signed property deed, because the signed physical document may be required for legal reasons.
The weekly staff lunch menu, because paper is cheaper than electricity.
The office's e-mail newsletter, because e-mails cannot be saved electronically.

questions.topic: Types of documents used in data processing
questions.stem:
These documents all pass through businesses in Grenada. Sort each one by the role it plays.

Which type of document is this?

A handwritten job application form for a summer job at a Grand Anse hotel.
questions.explain: The applicant's details are recorded here for the first time, so it is a source document.

questions.topic: Types of documents used in data processing
questions.stem:
Which type of document is this?

The barcode on a pack of rice at the supermarket.
questions.explain: The scanner reads the barcode directly, so it is machine-readable.

questions.topic: Types of documents used in data processing
questions.stem:
Which type of document is this?

A magazine renewal notice that the subscriber posts back with a cheque.
questions.explain: The system produced it, sent it out, and it returns as input. That is a turnaround document.

questions.topic: Types of documents used in data processing
questions.stem:
Which type of document is this?

A worker's weekly timesheet filled in by hand.
questions.explain: Hours are first written on the timesheet before payroll keys them in.

questions.topic: Types of documents used in data processing
questions.stem:
Which type of document is this?

A QR code on a ferry ticket to Carriacou.
questions.explain: A scanner reads the QR code directly.

questions.topic: Types of documents used in data processing
questions.stem:
Which type of document is this?

The stub of an electricity bill returned with the payment.
questions.explain: The stub was printed by the system and returned for further processing.

questions.topic: Types of documents used in data processing
questions.stem:
Which type of document is this?

A completed order form from a restaurant to its fish supplier.
questions.explain: The order data is first recorded on this form.

questions.topic: Types of documents used in data processing
questions.stem:
Which type of document is this?

An OMR answer sheet with shaded bubbles.
questions.explain: An optical mark reader reads the bubbles directly.

questions.topic: Types of documents used in data processing
questions.stem: Which of the following is BEST described as a machine-readable document?
options: A letter from a customer complaining about a delivery.
An OMR answer sheet with shaded bubbles.
A handwritten sales slip from a market vendor.

questions.stem:
You are on work experience at the Sunset Tours office in Speightstown. The manager says, "No one can find anything on our shared drive. Can you organise it?"

There are 200 files saved loosely on the shared drive with names like 'Document7'. Where do you begin?
options: Delete any file you do not recognise.
Create one folder called 'Old Stuff' and drag everything into it.
Plan a simple hierarchy first: folders for Bookings, Finance, Marketing and Staff, with sub-folders by year.

questions.stem: Your plan is ready. The manager suggests adding sub-folders by year, then by month, then by week, then by day, then by tour. What do you advise?
options: Suggest a shallow structure (folder > year) and put the date in the file name instead, using YYYY-MM-DD.
Agree. More levels always make things easier to find.

questions.stem: You start renaming files. How do you name them?
options: Let each staff member name files in whatever way they like.
Use a consistent convention, e.g. '2026-07-14 Booking Rivera', and write the rule down for all staff.

questions.topic: Issues related to the integrity of files
questions.stem:
Choose the MOST appropriate integrity measure for each situation at Port Elizabeth Shipping Agency.

The finance manager carries client accounts on a laptop that she takes to meetings in Kingstown. If it is stolen, the data must be unreadable.
questions.explain: Encryption keeps the content coded and unreadable without the key, even if the laptop is stolen.

questions.topic: Issues related to the integrity of files
questions.stem: A clerk saved this week's cargo list with last week's name, and last week's list disappeared.
questions.explain: Overwrite protection warns before an existing file is replaced by one with the same name.

questions.topic: Issues related to the integrity of files
questions.stem: Only the two directors should be able to open the salary spreadsheet.
questions.explain: Restricted access limits who may open, edit or delete the file through user accounts and permissions.

questions.topic: Issues related to the integrity of files
questions.stem: After a staff member opened an attachment called 'invoice.exe', several files became corrupted.
questions.explain: Virus protection detects, blocks and removes malicious programs before they can corrupt files.

questions.topic: Issues related to the integrity of files
questions.stem: All staff should be able to read the shipping safety procedures but no one should be able to edit them.
questions.explain: Read-only access lets everyone view the procedures while preventing changes.

questions.topic: Issues related to the integrity of files
questions.stem: A company wants staff to be able to VIEW the current staff handbook but not accidentally change it. Which file integrity measure is MOST appropriate?
options: Restricted access, so that only the HR manager can open it

questions.topic: Issues related to the integrity of files
questions.stem:
You work in the office of the Island Breeze Hotel in Ocho Rios. The reservations team uses a shared folder on the network.

Monday morning: the new room-rate list has vanished. A colleague saved a draft over it using the same name, 'Room Rates.xlsx'. What do you recommend first?
options: Tell everyone to be more careful.
Make sure the overwrite warning is switched on and that staff read it, and make the final rate list read-only.

questions.topic: Issues related to the integrity of files
questions.stem: The manager also wants to stop part-time staff from opening the folder that contains corporate discount contracts. What do you suggest?
options: Restrict access to that folder so only permanent reservations staff and the manager have permission.
Make the contracts read-only for everyone.

questions.topic: Issues related to the integrity of files
questions.stem: Finally, a guest e-mails a "booking form" attachment ending in '.exe'. A colleague is about to open it. What do you do?
options: Open it. It is probably just a booking.
Stop them. Scan it with up-to-date antivirus software, and do not open unexpected program files.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem:
The Frigate Bay Marine Supplies is reviewing its file security. Sort each measure.

Is this a cyber security measure, a physical security measure, or both?

A firewall on the office network.
questions.explain: A firewall controls network traffic. It is a cyber measure.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem:
Is this a cyber security measure, a physical security measure, or both?

A fireproof safe for original contracts.
questions.explain: Fireproof storage protects physical records from fire.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem:
Is this a cyber security measure, a physical security measure, or both?

Strong, unique passwords on every computer.
questions.explain: Passwords authenticate users digitally. Cyber.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem:
Is this a cyber security measure, a physical security measure, or both?

A waterproof cabinet raised off the floor of the storeroom.
questions.explain: Waterproof storage protects against flooding. Physical.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem:
Is this a cyber security measure, a physical security measure, or both?

Regular backup copies of all files.
questions.explain: Backup systems appear under both: digital copies protect against cyberattack, and off-site copies protect against physical disaster.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem:
Is this a cyber security measure, a physical security measure, or both?

A written disaster recovery plan.
questions.explain: Disaster recovery mechanisms appear under both cyber and physical security.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem:
Is this a cyber security measure, a physical security measure, or both?

A locked server room.
questions.explain: A lock protects the hardware physically.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem:
Is this a cyber security measure, a physical security measure, or both?

Antivirus software that blocks a malware attack.
questions.explain: Software protection against malicious programs is a cyber measure.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem: A business backs up its files only to a second hard drive kept in the same office. This practice is a weakness in...
options: both cyber and physical security, since a single disaster could destroy both copies.
cyber security only, with no physical security risk.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem:
It is September. A hurricane watch has been issued for St. Kitts, and you help the manager of the Sandy Point Accounting Services prepare the office.

The office's client files are on one desktop computer, with a backup on an external drive in the same room. What do you do first?
options: Check that a current backup also exists off-site, for example in cloud storage, and run a fresh backup now.
Put the external drive on top of the computer so they are together.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem: Next, the paper files: original signed tax forms and client agreements. Where should they go?
options: Into the fireproof and waterproof safe, raised off the floor, away from windows.
Leave them in the cardboard boxes under the desk.

questions.topic: Physical and cyber security of files
questions.stem: The storm passes, but the office has no power for a week and the computer is damaged. What now?
options: Follow the disaster recovery plan: restore the files from the cloud backup onto a laptop at a temporary location.
Close the business until the office is repaired, because the data is gone.

questions.topic: Retention of files and tracing document versions
questions.stem:
You help the May Pen Auto Parts office apply its retention schedule.

Last month's sales invoices, still used every week to answer customer queries.
questions.explain: They are still in active use, so they stay in active storage.

questions.topic: Retention of files and tracing document versions
questions.stem: Tax records from three years ago, rarely looked at but still within the legal minimum period.
questions.explain: They must still be kept by law, but they are rarely used, so they are archived.

questions.topic: Retention of files and tracing document versions
questions.stem: Customer records whose retention period ended last year and which contain credit-card slips.
options: dispose of securely, e.g. by shredding
questions.explain: The retention period has ended, and they contain sensitive data, so they must be disposed of securely.

questions.topic: Retention of files and tracing document versions
questions.stem: A notice about a staff meeting that took place two weeks ago.
questions.explain: It has no further use or legal value, so it can be deleted.

questions.topic: Retention of files and tracing document versions
questions.stem: Why should the old office computer's hard drive be wiped or destroyed before it is thrown away?
options: because ordinary deletion can often be undone, leaving data accessible
questions.explain: Deleted files can often be recovered. Secure disposal ensures sensitive information is not left accessible.

questions.topic: Retention of files and tracing document versions
questions.stem: A teacher opened a shared file of exam marks on Monday to read it, but did not change anything. The last change to the marks was made on the previous Friday. Which metadata field shows Monday's date?

questions.topic: Intellectual property and the rights it protects
questions.stem:
Read each situation and decide which right has been violated.

Which right is violated?

A radio station broadcasts a soca song every day without paying the songwriter any royalties.
questions.explain: The song is used commercially without payment. That is an economic right.

questions.topic: Intellectual property and the rights it protects
questions.stem:
Which right is violated?

A newspaper misquotes a scientist so that she appears to say the reef is healthy when she said it is in danger.
questions.explain: Misquoting damages her reputation and the integrity of her work. That is a moral right.

questions.topic: Intellectual property and the rights it protects
questions.stem:
Which right is violated?

A souvenir shop prints a photographer's picture on T-shirts and sells them, without paying her.
questions.explain: Commercial use without payment violates her economic right.

questions.topic: Intellectual property and the rights it protects
questions.stem:
Which right is violated?

A company crops out half of an artist's painting for an advert and changes its colours without asking her.
questions.explain: Altering the work without consent damages its integrity. That is a moral right (the company may have paid for the image).

questions.topic: Intellectual property and the rights it protects
questions.stem:
Which right is violated?

A website copies a poet's work, changes several lines, puts her name on it and sells it as an e-book without paying her.
questions.explain: She was not paid (economic) AND her work was altered under her name (moral). Both rights are violated.

questions.topic: Intellectual property and the rights it protects
questions.stem:
Which right is violated?

A school band records a cover of a local artist's song and sells the CDs at a fair, without a licence.
questions.explain: Selling copies of someone's song without a licence or payment violates economic rights.

questions.topic: Intellectual property and the rights it protects
questions.stem:
Which right is violated?

A blogger posts a journalist's article but names a different writer as the author, and sells advertising on the page.
questions.explain: Wrong author (misrepresentation, moral) and money made from the work without payment (economic).

questions.topic: Intellectual property and the rights it protects
questions.stem: A magazine reprints a photographer's image without payment, but credits the photographer accurately and does not alter the image in any way. Which right has been violated?
options: No rights, because she was credited

questions.topic: Copyright, open resources and ethical use
questions.stem:
The band Island Pulse has recorded a new album. Decide which party is described in each statement.

Island Pulse writes and records the songs and keeps ownership of them.
questions.explain: The band created the work and keeps control over it, so it is the producer/owner.

questions.topic: Copyright, open resources and ethical use
questions.stem: A record label signs an agreement with the band to press CDs and stream the album, and collects payments for them.
questions.explain: Entering agreements to record and distribute, and securing the producer's financial interests, is the publisher/distributor's role.

questions.topic: Copyright, open resources and ethical use
questions.stem: A DJ at a Port of Spain club asks the label for a licence to play the album at events.
questions.explain: The DJ is using the work and seeking permission through the publisher, so he is a consumer/user.

questions.topic: Copyright, open resources and ethical use
questions.stem: The label refuses to let a company use one song in an advert that would make the band look bad.
questions.explain: Publishers distribute work in ways that prevent unethical use of the material and protect the producer.

questions.topic: Copyright, open resources and ethical use
questions.stem: A student quotes one line of a song in her SBA and names the band and album in her reference list.
questions.explain: As a consumer/user, she has met her duty to acknowledge the source.

questions.topic: Copyright, open resources and ethical use
questions.stem: You find a perfect photo marked CC BY-NC. Another one is marked CC BY. The magazine will be sold. Which do you choose?
options: The CC BY-NC photo. It is for a school, so it does not count as commercial.
The CC BY photo, because it allows commercial use as long as the creator is credited.

questions.topic: Copyright, open resources and ethical use
questions.stem: The cover is ready. Where and how will you credit the photographer?
options: Print the photographer's name, the photo title, the source and "CC BY" on the inside cover credits.
Leave the credit out. It spoils the cover design.

questions.topic: Plagiarism and how to avoid it
questions.stem:
Students at Seagrape Bay Secondary School are preparing their EDPM SBA documents. Sort each action.

Is this plagiarism?

Ayana copies a paragraph from a website, puts it in quotation marks and adds an in-text citation.
questions.explain: Quotation marks plus a citation give the author appropriate credit.

questions.topic: Plagiarism and how to avoid it
questions.stem:
Is this plagiarism?

Jaden pastes a pie chart from a government report into his document with no source line.
questions.explain: Presenting someone else's data or image without credit is plagiarism.

questions.topic: Plagiarism and how to avoid it
questions.stem:
Is this plagiarism?

Mia rewrites an article's ideas fully in her own words and cites the article.
questions.explain: A thorough paraphrase with a citation is good practice.

questions.topic: Plagiarism and how to avoid it
questions.stem:
Is this plagiarism?

Tyrese changes a few words in each sentence of a textbook paragraph and gives no source.
questions.explain: Close paraphrasing without acknowledgement is plagiarism.

questions.topic: Plagiarism and how to avoid it
questions.stem:
Is this plagiarism?

Kezia lists every website and book she used in a reference list at the end.
questions.explain: A reference list acknowledges all sources consulted.

questions.topic: Plagiarism and how to avoid it
questions.stem:
Is this plagiarism?

Andre submits his cousin's typed letter from last year with his own name on it.
questions.explain: Presenting someone else's work as your own is plagiarism.

questions.topic: Plagiarism and how to avoid it
questions.stem:
Is this plagiarism?

Shanice hands in the same essay she wrote for Business Studies, without telling her EDPM teacher.
questions.explain: This is self-plagiarism: reusing her own previous work without acknowledging it.

questions.topic: Plagiarism and how to avoid it
questions.stem:
Is this plagiarism?

Rohan writes to a photographer, gets permission to use her photo, and credits her under it.
questions.explain: Obtaining approval and giving credit is exactly right.

questions.topic: Plagiarism and how to avoid it
questions.stem: Which of the following BEST explains why self-plagiarism is considered an ethical issue?
options: Your own work becomes the property of the school once it is marked.
It is only wrong if the old work received a low mark.
It misleads the reader or evaluator into believing the work is entirely new and original.
It violates the economic rights of another author.

questions.topic: Ordering priorities for acceptable standards of work
questions.stem:
You are an office assistant at the Harbour Light Printing in Bridgetown. On Monday the manager asks you to prepare a price list for a hotel client, due Friday at noon.

It is Monday afternoon. You also have routine filing and phone duties. What do you do with the price list?
options: Leave it until Thursday night. Friday is ages away.
Plan it: list the steps, block time on Tuesday and Wednesday, and keep Thursday for checking.

questions.topic: Ordering priorities for acceptable standards of work
questions.stem: On Wednesday you need last year's prices, but the file is not in the folder where it should be. What now?
options: Search the shared drive, find it misnamed as "New Doc 3", rename and file it correctly, then continue.
Guess the old prices from memory to save time.

questions.topic: Ordering priorities for acceptable standards of work
questions.stem: On Friday at 10:00 a.m. you e-mail the price list as a PDF to the hotel, as requested. What do you do next?
options: Check later that morning that the hotel received the file and that it opens correctly, and let your manager know.
Nothing. Once it is sent, it is their problem.

questions.topic: Ordering priorities for acceptable standards of work
questions.stem:
Each situation shows a problem at work or school. Choose the priority that was neglected.

A secretary cannot find a signed contract because papers are piled on her desk.
questions.explain: A disorganised workstation makes materials hard to find.

questions.topic: Ordering priorities for acceptable standards of work
questions.stem: A student uploads a Word file when the teacher asked for a PDF.
questions.explain: Submission must be in the format and manner specified.

questions.topic: Ordering priorities for acceptable standards of work
questions.stem: A clerk starts a 20-page report the night before it is due and has no time to proofread.
questions.explain: Effective time management leaves time for review and correction.

questions.topic: Ordering priorities for acceptable standards of work
questions.stem: An assistant asks a courier to deliver documents and never checks if they arrived. They did not.
questions.explain: Follow-up means checking back to confirm a task was completed.

questions.topic: Ordering priorities for acceptable standards of work
questions.stem: A student saves every file as "Document1", "Document2" and sends the wrong draft.
questions.explain: Meaningful file names are part of organising your digital workstation.

questions.stem:
Sort each online action by staff and students around Jamaica.

Is this appropriate online behaviour?

Before sending a staff e-mail, a clerk checks she has not clicked "Reply All" by mistake.
questions.explain: Think and check before sending, including recipients.

questions.stem:
Is this appropriate online behaviour?

A gamer types threats at an opponent after losing a match.
questions.explain: Hostile, threatening language is never acceptable, even in gaming.

questions.stem:
Is this appropriate online behaviour?

A blogger credits the photographer under a picture of Montego Bay Beach.
questions.explain: Citing sources online is a rule of conduct.

questions.stem:
Is this appropriate online behaviour?

A student posts a classmate's embarrassing photo without asking.
questions.explain: Unauthorised sharing of someone else's content.

questions.stem:
Is this appropriate online behaviour?

A forum user disagrees with a post by saying "I see it differently, because..."
questions.explain: Respectful disagreement focuses on ideas, not people.

questions.stem:
Is this appropriate online behaviour?

An employee replies to a client's complaint in ALL CAPITALS.
questions.explain: All capitals reads as shouting; it is discourteous.

questions.stem:
Is this appropriate online behaviour?

A student waits until he is calm before replying to a rude comment.
questions.explain: Thinking before sending prevents messages you will regret.

questions.stem:
Is this appropriate online behaviour?

A user posts deliberately provocative comments under a news story to start arguments.
questions.explain: These are inflammatory comments.

questions.stem:
You are in a Form 5 group chat. Late one evening, a classmate posts a screenshot of a private message from Jada, along with jokes about her.

Several people are already replying with laughing emojis. What do you do?
options: Do not join in, and post: "This was a private message. Please delete it."
Add a funny comment of your own. Everyone else is doing it.

questions.stem: The next day the same classmate posts another joke about Jada, and then another. It is clearly becoming a pattern. What now?
options: Reply with insults about the classmate to defend Jada.
Take screenshots of the posts with dates and report it to your form teacher or the guidance counsellor.

questions.stem: Jada messages you privately to thank you. She asks if you can forward the screenshots to her so she has them. What do you do?
options: Post all the screenshots on your public social media page so everyone sees what the bully did.
Send them privately to Jada only, and remind her that the teacher is already handling it.

questions.stem: An office assistant receives an angry e-mail from a customer. Which of the following actions BEST follows the netiquette rule "think and check before sending"?
options: Draft a calm reply, re-read it for content, tone and recipients, and then send it.
Post the e-mail on the company's social media page so the public can judge.
Forward the e-mail to all staff with a joke about the customer.
Reply immediately in capital letters so the customer knows the company is serious.

questions.stem:
Staff at the Bayview Travel are showing good attitudes. Sort each action to the attitude it shows MOST clearly.

Which attitude is shown most clearly?

Asked to learn the new booking software, Jerome says, "Happy to. When is the training?"
questions.explain: Readily accepting a new task without complaint is willingness.

questions.stem:
Which attitude is shown most clearly?

With the supervisor off sick, Leah completes the week's invoices accurately and on time.
questions.explain: Completing work to standard without supervision is individual responsibility.

questions.stem:
Which attitude is shown most clearly?

Marcus admits that he entered a wrong date on a ticket, although nobody had noticed.
questions.explain: Being honest when no one is checking is personal integrity.

questions.stem:
Which attitude is shown most clearly?

Nadia offers to help a colleague prepare for a trade show without being asked twice.
questions.explain: Readiness to take on extra responsibility is willingness.

questions.stem:
Which attitude is shown most clearly?

Working from home, Ana checks and files every client e-mail before logging off, although no one monitors her.
questions.explain: Reliable work without direct oversight is individual responsibility.

questions.stem:
Which attitude is shown most clearly?

Jerome refuses to change a customer review to make the company look better.
questions.explain: Refusing to be dishonest is personal integrity.

questions.stem:
Which attitude is shown most clearly?

Leah agrees to take on the extra Saturday shift during Carnival week without grumbling.
questions.explain: Accepting a task without excessive reluctance is willingness.

questions.stem:
Read each situation and choose the desirable habit or work attitude that is MOST directly shown or neglected.

A new employee from the Dominican Republic is helped by colleagues who learn a few Spanish greetings to make her welcome.
questions.explain: Valuing people of different backgrounds and cultures is recognition of and respect for diversity.

questions.stem: A clerk is late three days out of five.
questions.explain: Being consistently on time is punctuality and regularity, which he is neglecting.

questions.stem: A designer refuses to share the shared template with the rest of the team, so others have to redo work.
questions.explain: Sharing information and resources appropriately is co-operation, which is missing here.

questions.stem: An assistant joins a video meeting late, with her camera off and loud music in the background.
questions.explain: Professional conduct in virtual meetings is remote working etiquette.

questions.stem: A receptionist interrupts and rolls her eyes while a client explains a problem.
questions.explain: Polite, considerate behaviour is courtesy, which is missing here.

questions.stem: An employee always delivers the weekly report by the agreed Wednesday time.
questions.explain: Completing work within the agreed time frame is meeting deadlines.

questions.stem: Kayla works from home for a Nassau insurance office. Which of the following BEST shows remote working etiquette?
options: She logs on whenever she feels like it, as long as the work gets done eventually.
She attends video meetings in pyjamas with her camera off, because no one can see her anyway.
She forwards client files to her personal e-mail so she can work on them more easily.
She joins video meetings on time from a quiet space, mutes when not speaking and replies to e-mails promptly and clearly.
